title: Docs: conflicting descriptions of the private flag for realtime.send / realtime.send_binary
body:
## Page

https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime/broadcast#broadcast-from-the-database

Source: `apps/docs/content/guides/realtime/broadcast.mdx`

## Problem

The `private` argument gets three different labels on this page, and two of them are reversed:

- `realtime.send` example: `false -- Public / Private flag`
- `realtime.send_binary` example: `true -- Private / Public flag (defaults to true)`
- "Broadcasting a message from your database" section: `FALSE -- Public / Private flag`

None of them say what `true` and `false` do. `private` is a positional boolean, so a wrong value changes whether the message needs channel authorization, and a public message never reaches a private channel.

The note near the top of the page also calls it "the public flag" while the parameter is named `private`:

> The public flag (the last argument in `realtime.send(payload, event, topic, is_private)`) only affects who can subscribe to the topic not who can read messages from the database.

That note explains the values correctly. The inline comments in the examples contradict it.

## Ground truth

Both functions declare the argument the same way:

```sql
create or replace function realtime.send (
  payload jsonb,
  event   text,
  topic   text,
  private boolean default true
)
```

`private => true` sends on a private channel. `private => false` sends on a public channel. The default is `true`.

## Fix

- Use one label for the parameter in all three SQL examples.
- State what the values do, for example `-- private: true = private channel (default), false = public channel`.
- Show the `true` default in the `realtime.send` example too.
- Call it "the `private` flag" in the note, to match the parameter name.
- Consider [named notation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-syntax-calling-funcs.html#SQL-SYNTAX-CALLING-FUNCS-NAMED) in the examples, so the call documents itself:

```sql
select realtime.send(
  payload => jsonb_build_object('hello', 'world'),
  event   => 'event',
  topic   => 'topic',
  private => true
);
```

Ref REAL-1051

title: PGRST303 "JWT issued at future" with sb_secret_ keys — skew sometimes exceeds a 2s retry budget (adds details to #49655)
body:
### Summary

Server-side REST requests authenticated with the **new-format `sb_secret_` API key** intermittently fail with:

```
HTTP 401
PGRST303 — JWT issued at future
```

We never mint or send a JWT. The token being validated is created **inside Supabase** (the gateway exchanges the opaque `sb_secret_` key for a short-lived JWT before forwarding to PostgREST), so the `iat` being "in the future" can only mean clock skew between two Supabase components.

This has been reported twice before and both were closed as `awaiting-details`:

- supabase/supabase#49655 — same key format, same error
- supabase/supabase#41294 — more severe variant (PostgREST ~15h ahead)

This report adds the details those were missing: a **19-day timeline**, **HTTP-level evidence**, and a measurement showing the skew **sometimes exceeds 2 seconds**.

---

### What we send

| | |
|---|---|
| Client | `@supabase/supabase-js`, server-side (Node 26) |
| Auth | `sb_secret_…` key (new format, **not** a legacy JWT service key) |
| Token minted by us | **none** |
| Our host | Railway; our own clock shows no skew in our logs |

The key format carries no `iat` claim, so the rejected timestamp cannot be one we supplied.

---

### Timeline (all UTC)

**2026-09-02** — 5 × HTTP 500 out of 501 requests over a 5-hour window, across three different public pages. Several independent server-side reads (settings, regions, payment methods, one product table) all failed in the **same second** with the identical message. One failure was reproduced in a browser; the Next.js error digest shown to the visitor matched the server log exactly.

**2026-09-19 21:03:30** — public page → 500. Failing read was a `select` with an `!inner` join. Supabase returned **401 / PGRST303**.

**2026-09-20 11:12:29** — different public page → 500. Failing read was a simple single-table `select`. Same 401 / PGRST303.

Between those dates the error appeared only intermittently; it is not reproducible on demand, which is why this is a measurement report rather than a repro script.

---

### Sizing the skew

After the 2026-09-02 event we added a fetch-level retry that fires only on `401/403` **and** this specific body signature:

| | |
|---|---|
| Attempts | 4 |
| Backoff | 120 ms, 320 ms, 600 ms, 1000 ms (~2 s total budget) |

In one 11-minute window we observed **two** occurrences: one recovered inside the ~2 s budget, the other did **not**.

That is the part we think is new: #49655 reported recovery at ~1.4 s, which suggests sub-second skew. **We have at least one occurrence where the skew outlived a 2-second retry budget.**

---

### Impact

Public, crawlable pages returned HTTP 500 to real visitors and to search-engine crawlers. The failure is transient and unpredictable, so it is invisible to uptime checks that sample infrequently.

---

### Questions

1. Can you confirm whether NTP skew between the API gateway and PostgREST is known on the affected instances, and whether there is a fix in progress?
2. `PGRST303` says "JWT issued at future" even when the caller supplied a **non-JWT** `sb_secret_` key. Could the message distinguish *gateway-minted* tokens from caller-supplied ones? Right now users cannot tell "your clock" from "our clock", which is likely why the earlier reports were closed as external.
3. Is there a supported client-side leeway/tolerance setting, or is retrying the only mitigation available to users?

---

### Mitigations we shipped (context, not a fix request)

- Fetch-level retry on this exact signature (above)
- Config reads fall back to the last known-good snapshot for up to 5 minutes
- One cached page serves its existing snapshot instead of a 500 when this specific error occurs

None address the cause. Happy to supply request IDs and exact timestamps privately for a specific project ref if that helps.

title: Webhook Permissions Error Referring to Type in Extensions Schema
body:
# Bug report
If a web hook is set on a table where one of the types used in that table is defined in a separate schema e.g. `extensions`, an exception is raised


Reproduction Steps:

1. Enable PostGIS extension in Studio in the `extensions schema`

2. Create a table with a Point type: `create table geom (coordinates extensions.geometry(Point, 4326))`;

2. Create am `insert` webhook for the `public.geom` table

3. Insert a row in the table
```sql
insert into  geom(coordinates)
values(ST_GeomFromText('POINT(-71.060316 48.432044)', 4326));
```

Error
```
permission denied for schema extensions
```

----
The line in the `supabase_functions.http_request` that raises the exception is
https://github.com/supabase/supabase/blob/aed59dd84f2a656dc5a7669b47bce8920d417d39/docker/volumes/db/webhooks.sql#L76-L82

You can confirm that by chopping everything else out of that trigger function and seeing that the issue persists
```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION supabase_functions.http_request()
    RETURNS trigger
    LANGUAGE 'plpgsql'
    VOLATILE NOT LEAKPROOF SECURITY DEFINER
    SET search_path=supabase_functions
AS $BODY$
    BEGIN
	  raise exception 'asdf %', current_role;
      perform jsonb_build_object(
            'old_record', OLD,
            'record', NEW,
            'type', TG_OP,
            'table', TG_TABLE_NAME,
            'schema', TG_TABLE_SCHEMA
          );
      RETURN NEW;
    END
$BODY$;
```

title: Self-Hosted: JWT config applied to wrong database when using custom POSTGRES_DB
body:
### Bug description
I was setting up a self-hosted instance and wanted to use a custom database name instead of the default `postgres`. After changing `POSTGRES_DB` in my `.env` file, I noticed that auth and RLS weren't working correctly. 

I dug into the Docker initialization scripts and found the culprit: `docker/volumes/db/jwt.sql` completely ignores the `POSTGRES_DB` environment variable and hardcodes the database name:

```sql
ALTER DATABASE postgres SET "app.settings.jwt_exp" TO :'jwt_exp';
If anyone overrides POSTGRES_DB (which is officially supported in CONFIG.md), their JWT configs get applied to the wrong database and auth fails silently.

Expected behavior
jwt.sql should read the POSTGRES_DB environment variable and apply the settings to that database.
```
### Reproducing steps
Change POSTGRES_DB=custom_db in .env.
Run docker compose up -d.
Check custom_db for app.settings.jwt_exp — it will be missing because it was applied to postgres instead.

title: Storage API: Case-sensitive "Content-Type" header causes multipart boundary storage instead of file content
body:
Supabase storage API stores multipart form data boundaries instead of actual file content when using capitalized "Content-Type" header. Files upload successfully (200 OK) but contain the entire multipart envelope rather than just the file bytes.

Upload file using capitalized header:

```python
# ❌ This causes the issue
headers = {"Content-Type": file.content_type, "upsert": "true"}
```

File gets stored with multipart boundaries:
```
--boundary123\r\nContent-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="test.pdf"\r\nContent-Type: application/pdf\r\n\r\n%PDF-1.4...
```

Downloads return malformed content instead of actual file

**Expected behavior**
File should be stored with just the file content, regardless of header capitalization.

**Actual behavior**
- Capitalized "Content-Type": Stores multipart boundaries ❌
- Lowercase "content-type": Stores file content correctly ✅


**Environment**

Supabase Python client: v2.17.0
Environment: Local development
Python version: 3.12.11

**Additional context**

- **_HTTP RFC states headers should be case-insensitive_**
- This affects both Python client and direct REST API calls
- Related to multipart form parsing in storage backend
- No error thrown - files appear to upload successfully but contain wrong data

**Minimal Replication**

```python
from fastapi import UploadFile
from supabase import create_client

# This breaks
result = supabase.storage.from_("bucket").upload(
    filename, 
    file_content,
    file_options={"Content-Type": file.content_type}  # ❌
)

# This works  
result = supabase.storage.from_("bucket").upload(
    filename,
    file_content, 
    file_options={"content-type": file.content_type}  # ✅
)
```

title: Preview branches do not preserve object privileges in public, and do not create auth.users triggers
body:
## Summary

Creating a preview branch produces a database whose **schema** matches its parent but whose **privileges and
`auth`-schema triggers do not**. Two distinct losses, measured, reproducible on every branch we create:

1. **Object privileges are not preserved.** `GRANT`/`REVOKE` state on `public` functions and tables is
   replaced by what the schema's default privileges produce, so roles hold access the parent revoked.
2. **Triggers on `auth.users` are not created.** A trigger the parent carries is simply absent.

The first is a security-relevant divergence: on our branches `anon` holds every privilege on tables the parent
revokes it from, and `authenticated` can execute functions the parent restricts to `service_role`.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Branch created via | `POST /v1/branches` (Management API), `with_data: false` |
| Instance size | `ci_micro` |
| PostgreSQL | 17.6 |
| Schema size | 285 migrations · 385 `public` functions · 98 `public` tables · 118 RLS policies |

## Defect 1 — object privileges are not preserved

### Expected

A branch's `public` objects carry the same `relacl` / `proacl` as the parent's.

### Actual

They carry what the schema's default privileges produce. Measured on a fresh branch, comparing raw ACLs:

| object class | rows compared | differ from parent |
|---|---|---|
| function ACLs | 385 | **204** |
| table ACLs | 98 | **45** |

Representative examples — parent first, branch second:

```
activate_tenant(uuid)
  parent: postgres=X/postgres, service_role=X/postgres
  branch: postgres=X/postgres, anon=X/postgres, authenticated=X/postgres, service_role=X/postgres

contacts
  parent: postgres=arwdDxtm, authenticated=arwdDxtm, service_role=arwdDxtm
  branch: … plus anon=arwdDxtm          ← every privilege, on a table the parent revokes anon from

call_disposition_catalog
  parent: authenticated=r               ← read only
  branch: authenticated=arwdDxtm        ← full write
```

### What IS preserved

Worth stating, because it narrows the cause: **row-level security is intact.** Comparing parent to branch:

| dimension | differences |
|---|---|
| RLS enabled / forced | **0** |
| RLS policies (118) | **0** |
| schema `USAGE` on `public` | **0** |
| sequence ACLs | **0** |
| default ACLs in `public` | **0** |

So policies survive; the grants beneath them do not. Where RLS also applies, table access still narrows by
tenant — but **functions have no RLS**, so for functions the loss is unmitigated.

### Likely mechanism

Consistent with objects being **recreated as `postgres`** during branch provisioning, allowing `public`'s
default privileges to apply, with the parent's explicit `GRANT`/`REVOKE` state not replayed afterwards.

⚠ Two candidate causes we **ruled out by measurement**, in case they save you time:

- **It is not `PUBLIC`.** The raw ACLs name `anon` and `authenticated` explicitly, granted by `postgres`.
- **It is not a default-ACL difference in `public`.** Those are identical between parent and branch (24 rows
  each). The branch has **three extra** `pg_default_acl` rows, all in the **`supabase_functions`** schema,
  which appear to be ordinary platform provisioning and unrelated.

## Defect 2 — triggers on `auth.users` are not created

### Expected

A trigger the parent has on `auth.users` exists on the branch.

### Actual

It is absent.

```
auth-schema triggers    parent: 1    branch: 0
  parent has, branch lacks:
    users :: on_auth_user_created -> handle_new_user (AFTER INSERT, enabled=O)
```

The trigger is created by one of our migrations:

```sql
create trigger on_auth_user_created
  after insert on auth.users
  for each row execute function handle_new_user();
```

### Impact

Signup does not produce the row the trigger exists to create, so any test of post-signup behaviour fails on a
branch while passing against the parent. This is the failure that led us to look: an end-to-end test asserting
that a profile row appears after `auth.admin.createUser` returns **PGRST116 — "The result contains 0 rows"**.

## Reproduction

1. On a project with non-default grants in `public` and a trigger on `auth.users`, create a branch:
   `POST /v1/branches` with `with_data: false`.
2. Wait for the branch to reach a settled state. ⚠ `ACTIVE_HEALTHY` is **not** terminal — we observe
   `… → ACTIVE_HEALTHY → RESTORING → ACTIVE_HEALTHY`, and reading at the first one returns zeros.
3. Connect to the branch and to the parent, and compare:

```sql
-- privileges (run against both, then diff)
select p.oid::regprocedure::text, coalesce(array_to_string(p.proacl::text[], ','), 'NULL')
  from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace
 where n.nspname = 'public' and p.prokind = 'f' order by 1;

select c.relname, coalesce(array_to_string(c.relacl::text[], ','), 'NULL')
  from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
 where n.nspname = 'public' and c.relkind = 'r' order by 1;

-- auth triggers (run against both)
select c.relname, t.tgname, p.proname
  from pg_trigger t
  join pg_class c on c.oid = t.tgrelid
  join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
  join pg_proc p on p.oid = t.tgfoid
 where n.nspname = 'auth' and not t.tgisinternal;
```

Both differences appear on every branch we have created. **Neither is intermittent**: the privilege figures
(204 / 45) were identical across four separate branches, and the missing trigger reproduced on every run.

## What we are doing meanwhile

Reconciling privileges after branch creation, from a schema built out of our own migrations. It works — it
took an end-to-end suite from 21 of 33 passing to 30 of 33 — but it is a workaround for something we would
rather not have to detect.

We have **not** recreated the `auth` trigger on a branch. Not because we believe it unsafe: our own migration
creates exactly that trigger on three ordinary projects, and the
[User Management guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/managing-user-data) documents the same pattern.
It is that a branch's schema does not appear to come from replaying our migrations, so the migration that
creates the trigger never runs there — which is what question 2 below is really asking about.

## Questions

**1. Is privilege loss on branch creation known, or expected behaviour we should design around?**

The closest statement we can find in the docs is
[Branching via the dashboard → Limitations](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/deployment/branching/dashboard#limitations):

> Custom roles created through the dashboard are not captured on branch creation

That is about **roles**. What we lose is **grants to the three built-in roles** — `anon`, `authenticated`,
`service_role` — on objects our own migrations create. If those are the same underlying behaviour, the
limitation as written is far narrower than what it covers.

**2. How is a branch's schema actually produced?**

The same Limitations list says:

> If you have run migrations on main, new branches will be created from existing migrations instead of a full
> schema dump

We have run migrations on main. On that description the branch is built by replaying them — and the migration
quoted under Defect 2 creates `on_auth_user_created`. It is not on the branch. Meanwhile the branch **does**
have all 385 functions and 98 tables those same migrations create, so the schema is reproduced somehow.

So one of these should be true, and which one decides whether Defect 2 shares a root cause with Defect 1:

- that statement describes dashboard branching only, and Management-API branches are produced another way;
- the replay happens but skips DDL targeting the `auth` schema;
- the replay happens as a role without `TRIGGER` on `auth.users`, and that one failure is swallowed.

The third would account for both defects at once — the branch being built by a role with different authority
than the parent's owner.

---

*Edited 2026-08-22: a third question — whether recreating a trigger on `auth.users` is safe — was removed. The
User Management guide documents that pattern, and we already do it on three non-branch projects, so it was not
ours to ask. Question 2 was rewritten to state the contradiction with the documented branch-creation mechanism
rather than to ask an open-ended "same root cause?".*

title: Preview branch migration runner corrupts newlines to literal 'n' characters
body:
- [x] I confirm this is a bug with Supabase, not with my own application.
- [x] I confirm I have searched the [Docs](https://docs.supabase.com), GitHub [Discussions](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/discussions), and [Discord](https://discord.supabase.com).

## Bug report

### Describe the bug

When Supabase preview branches run migrations, newline characters (`\n` / `0x0a`) in SQL migration files are being converted to the literal character `n`, causing syntax errors.

The migration file on disk has correct Unix line endings (verified via hex dump), but the preview branch migration runner corrupts them before executing.

### To Reproduce

1. Have a migration file with multi-line SQL statements (e.g., `CREATE TYPE ... AS ENUM` with values on separate lines)
2. Push a branch that triggers a preview branch creation
3. The preview branch migration runner fails with a syntax error

### Expected behavior

Migration files should be executed with their original newline characters preserved.

### Actual behavior

Newlines are stripped and replaced with the literal character `n`. For example, this valid SQL:

```sql
create type subscription_status as ENUM (
  'active',
  'trialing',
  'past_due'
);
```

Gets executed as:

```sql
create type subscription_status as ENUM (n  'active',n  'trialing',n  'past_due'n);
```

Resulting in:
```
ERROR: syntax error at or near "n" (SQLSTATE 42601)
```

### Screenshots / logs

From the preview branch workflow logs:

```
2026/02/09 13:55:39 ERROR: syntax error at or near "n" (SQLSTATE 42601)
At statement: 0
create type subscription_status as ENUM (n  'active',n  'trialing',n  'past_due',n  'canceled',n  'unpaid',n  'incomplete',n  'incomplete_expired',n  'paused'n)
                                         ^
```

### Hex dump of migration file (proving correct line endings)

```
00000020: 6173 2045 4e55 4d28 0a20 2027 6163 7469  as ENUM(.  'acti
00000030: 7665 272c 0a20 2027 7472 6961 6c69 6e67  ve',.  'trialing
```

`0a` = proper LF newline. The file is fine — the corruption happens in the migration runner.

### System information

- Supabase plan: Pro
- Feature: Preview branches (branching)
- Migration file encoding: ASCII with Unix (LF) line endings

### Additional context

This appears related to #35371. The issue affects any migration file with multi-line SQL statements when run through the preview branch system.

title: Branching: preview `migrate` step DIES on multi-migration gap; `supabase db push --include-all` applies the same gap cleanly
body:
## Summary

When a Supabase preview branch is created (either via GitHub integration on a PR or via Management API / MCP), it spawns with a **subset** of the parent project's migration history applied to the tracking table, then the preview-branching `migrate` step DIES trying to apply the gap. The same gap is applied without error by `supabase db push --include-all --linked` from the CLI against the same preview branch.

This generates spurious "⚠️ Service health check failed" comments on PR previews even though all services are healthy and our migrations are valid.

## Reproduction

Tested against project ref `byvleunmmqjfroztnqgy` (parent) on 2026-04-22.

1. Parent project has 25 migrations tracked in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`, earliest `20260417000000` (post-consolidation baseline), latest `20260422021351`. All migrations are committed and confirmed in sync via `supabase migration list --linked`.

2. Created a branch via Management API:
   ```bash
   curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPABASE_TOKEN" \
     "https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/byvleunmmqjfroztnqgy/branches" \
     -d '{"branch_name":"health-probe-investigation"}'
   # → branch ref: cfwtrulhimxjapemejyd
   ```

3. Polled `/v1/projects/{preview_ref}/actions`:
   ```
   clone:     EXITED   ✅
   pull:      EXITED   ✅
   health:    EXITED   ✅
   configure: EXITED   ✅
   migrate:   DEAD     ❌
   seed:      CREATED  (skipped)
   deploy:    CREATED  (skipped)
   ```

4. Queried preview's tracking table:
   ```sql
   SELECT COUNT(*), MIN(version), MAX(version) FROM supabase_migrations.schema_migrations;
   -- 9, 20260417000000, 20260419010459
   ```
   Preview was tracking only 9 of the parent's 25 migrations — missing the latest 16.

5. Verified missing-migration artifacts were absent: tables/enums introduced by the 16 missing migrations did NOT exist on the preview, and a column dropped by one of them was still present. Preview's data state was consistent with its tracking — i.e., the gap migrations had not been partially applied.

6. Ran the same migrations via local CLI:
   ```bash
   supabase link --project-ref cfwtrulhimxjapemejyd
   supabase db push --include-all --linked
   # → Applied all 16 missing migrations cleanly
   # → "Finished supabase db push" with no errors
   ```

7. Re-queried preview's tracking table: now `25` rows. Schema artifacts now match parent.

## Logs endpoint returns ResourceNotFoundException

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPABASE_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/cfwtrulhimxjapemejyd/actions/cfwtrulhimxjapemejyd/logs"

# → {"message":"failed to stream logs: operation error CloudWatch Logs: GetLogEvents,
#     https response error StatusCode: 400, ResourceNotFoundException:
#     The specified log stream does not exist."}
```

This makes the failure undiagnosable from the dashboard for affected customers — the only way to find out what happened is to bypass and retry manually as I did.

## Service health is fine

The `/v1/projects/{preview_ref}/health?services=...` endpoint returned `healthy: true, status: ACTIVE_HEALTHY` for all 6 services (auth, db, pooler, realtime, rest, storage) at the time `migrate: DEAD` was reported. The bot comment's "Service health check failed" text is therefore misleading — the `health` step did pass. The actual failure is in the `migrate` step.

## Hypothesis

The preview-branching `migrate` agent appears to NOT use `--include-all` (or equivalent), so it bails on out-of-order timestamps that arise during normal multi-developer workflows. Out-of-order timestamps are common when concurrent branches generate migrations independently — Supabase's own docs even warn about this in the `db push` CLI context, but the branching agent doesn't seem to handle it the same way.

## Customer-side impact

PRs containing more than a few migrations beyond the preview snapshot point reliably trigger this. We've seen it on multiple PRs (#1480, #1521, plus the live repro above). Reviewers learn to ignore the ⚠️ which is exactly the wrong outcome — it trains the team to ignore yellow-flag warnings generally.

## Workaround

Add a GitHub Actions job that detects preview branch creation, fetches the preview ref via Management API, and runs `supabase db push --include-all --linked` to repair the migrate state. This is what we're implementing, but it's load-bearing tooling that customers shouldn't need.

## Asks

1. Make the preview-branching `migrate` step use the same migration apply logic as `supabase db push --include-all --linked`.
2. Fix the CloudWatch logs endpoint so `migrate: DEAD` runs surface their actual error to customers.
3. Update the bot comment text — when `migrate` fails, say "Migration apply failed" rather than "Service health check failed". The current text misdirects diagnosis.

Happy to provide more repro info, branch credentials for inspection (within a debug window), or anything else useful.

title: Branching: create_branch fails MIGRATIONS_FAILED when project history starts with a repair-marked (squashed) baseline
body:
### Describe the bug

Creating a branch on a project whose migration history begins with a squashed baseline that is *marked applied* on the remote history (the standard `db pull` → `migration repair --status applied` bootstrap) fails with `MIGRATIONS_FAILED`. The fresh branch records the baseline as applied in its migration ledger, but the baseline's DDL is never executed against the empty branch database — so the *next* migration runs against a schema that was never created and fails.

### Actual behavior

- Branch provisioning ends in `MIGRATIONS_FAILED`.
- The branch's ledger shows only the baseline as the last-applied migration.
- Postgres logs show the second migration failing: `relation "public.organizations" does not exist`.
- `public.organizations` is a table the **baseline itself creates** (`create table if not exists public.organizations (...)`) — confirming the baseline's SQL never ran on the branch; only its ledger entry was written.

### Expected behavior

On a fresh empty branch the baseline's SQL should be executed (or the branch seeded from a snapshot that already contains the baseline schema) before later migrations run. A migration should never be applied against a schema its skipped baseline was responsible for creating.

### To Reproduce

1. A project bootstrapped from an existing DB: one large squashed baseline migration marked already-applied on the remote history (`supabase migration repair --status applied <baseline>`), followed by incremental migrations that depend on tables the baseline creates.
2. Create a new branch (Management API / `create_branch` — a from-scratch replay onto an empty DB).
3. Provisioning fails: baseline recorded as applied but its DDL not run, so the first post-baseline migration hits a missing relation the baseline defines.

### Additional context

The identical history replays cleanly from empty via the CLI (`supabase start` / `supabase db reset`) **and** via GitHub-integration PR-triggered preview branches — so the migration files are self-consistent. Only the direct `create_branch` path fails, which points at how branch provisioning seeds/executes a pre-marked baseline on an empty database. (History here is a baseline + ~160 incremental migrations.)
qualityReasoning: Detailed issue description (2240 chars) with technical context, code/log references, and clear scope.

title: RLS INSERT policy rejects writes with provably-matching auth.uid(), unaffected by WITH CHECK (true) or a schema-cache reload — only resolved by disabling RLS
body:
We have a table public.event_registrations with RLS enabled. Its INSERT policy is:


CREATE POLICY "Users can register themselves for an event" ON event_registrations
  FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid());
A specific, real, authenticated user (auth.users.id = profiles.id = 6665dc44-4c42-4dc1-a028-df513af0a21e, confirmed identical by direct query) was consistently rejected trying to insert a row with user_id set to that exact same id, via our app's normal PostgREST-backed client (supabase-js .from("event_registrations").insert(...)), with:


ERROR: 42501: new row violates row-level security policy for table "event_registrations"
This reproduced on multiple separate accounts (both a brand-new Google OAuth signup and a pre-existing, long-logged-in email/password account), always for the same event, always with the exact same error.

What we ruled out, in order, each independently confirmed against the live database:

Client-side identity mismatch added logging comparing the exact value sent as user_id against (await supabase.auth.getSession()).data.session.user.id at the moment of the failing request. They matched exactly (full UUID, not truncated, no whitespace).
Wrong or missing policy select * from pg_policies where tablename='event_registrations' showed exactly the one INSERT policy above (plus a correct SELECT and DELETE policy), all permissive, no hidden restrictive policy.
RLS not actually enabled / forced incorrectly — select relrowsecurity, relforcerowsecurity from pg_class where relname='event_registrations' returned true, false enabled normally, not forced.
auth.uid()/profile id mismatch in the database — direct query confirmed auth.users.id = profiles.id for the affected account.
auth.uid() itself redefined/broken select pg_get_functiondef('auth.uid()'::regprocedure) returned Supabase's standard, unmodified implementation.
A trigger interfering one AFTER INSERT trigger exists (on_registration → update_attending_count()), confirmed SECURITY DEFINER, only touches the unrelated events table, matches our own tracked copy of its definition exactly.
The chained .select()/RETURNING clause failing under its own SELECT policy (a known RLS+RETURNING interaction) ruled out by testing a bare INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING with no RETURNING at all, direct in the SQL editor. Same error.
Missing/mismatched unique constraint backing our ON CONFLICT target confirmed a real UNIQUE (event_id, user_id) constraint exists.
A stale/unsettled client session right after a fresh sign-in added an explicit getSession() "prime" call plus an 800ms-delayed retry before the write. Same error on retry. Also reproduced on a long-established, already-logged-in session with no fresh sign-in involved at all.
Direct SQL impersonation, bypassing the network/client entirely from the SQL editor, in one atomic DO $$ ... $$ block (to avoid any SET LOCAL transaction-boundary ambiguity across separate statement round trips):

DO $$
DECLARE v_count int;
BEGIN
  SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated;
  PERFORM set_config('request.jwt.claims', '{"sub":"6665dc44-4c42-4dc1-a028-df513af0a21e","role":"authenticated"}', true);
  INSERT INTO event_registrations (user_id, event_id, paid)
  VALUES ('6665dc44-4c42-4dc1-a028-df513af0a21e', '1798b492-7f66-442d-b86b-3374f09597e6', false)
  ON CONFLICT (event_id, user_id) DO NOTHING;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_count = ROW_COUNT;
  RAISE EXCEPTION 'TEST RESULT: insert succeeded, rows inserted=%', v_count;
END $$;
Still failed with the same 42501 error, at the INSERT line specifically (confirmed via the error CONTEXT) — with role and JWT claim explicitly, correctly set to the exact id being inserted, in the same atomic block, no RETURNING involved.

Dropped and recreated the policy from scratch (in case of some internal state issue from an earlier automated policy rewrite that switched auth.uid() to (select auth.uid()) for the auth_rls_initplan performance advisory) — same error.
Replaced the policy entirely with WITH CHECK (true) a condition that cannot evaluate to false — via the actual app (not just SQL editor), and it produced the identical 42501 error again.
NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema' no change.
The only thing that resolved it was disabling RLS on the table entirely via the dashboard.

What we'd like from you: an explanation of what could cause step 12 in particular (a WITH CHECK (true) INSERT policy rejecting every insert) since that rules out our policy logic entirely and points at something below Postgres's own RLS evaluation on your platform (connection-pooler-level plan caching that a schema-cache reload doesn't invalidate, was our best guess, but we have no way to confirm that from our side). We've since worked around it by routing writes through a SECURITY DEFINER function instead of a direct table insert, which does work but we'd like to understand whether this could affect other tables/policies in this project too, since our workaround only fixes the one table we happened to catch it on.

title: API reference: 11 of 12 branching endpoints document only 500, and /diff is the only GET in v1 requiring a :write OAuth scope
body:
# Improve documentation

## Link

- https://supabase.com/docs/reference/api/v1-diff-a-branch
- https://supabase.com/docs/reference/api/v1-list-all-branches
- Source spec: `https://api.supabase.com/api/v1-json`

## Describe the problem

Two gaps in how the Branching surface of the Management API is described. Both come
from the OpenAPI spec that generates these reference pages, so they show up both in
the docs and in every client generated from the spec.

Filing together because they share a namespace (happy to split if you'd prefer).

### 1. Every branching endpoint documents `500` and nothing else — except one

Across the whole v1 spec, **151 of 169 operations** document `401`, `403` and `429`.
Inside the branching namespace that ratio inverts:

| Method | Path | Documented error responses |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}` | `500` |
| PATCH | `/v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}` | `500` |
| DELETE | `/v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}` | `500` |
| GET | `/v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}/diff` | `500` |
| POST | `/v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}/merge` | `500` |
| POST | `/v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}/push` | `500` |
| POST | `/v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}/reset` | `500` |
| POST | `/v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}/restore` | `500` |
| GET | `/v1/projects/{ref}/branches` | `500` |
| POST | `/v1/projects/{ref}/branches` | `500` |
| GET | `/v1/projects/{ref}/branches/{name}` | `500` |
| **DELETE** | **`/v1/projects/{ref}/branches`** | **`401`, `403`, `429`, `500`** |

The last row is the tell: one endpoint in the same namespace already carries the
full set, so this reads as drift rather than an intentional contract.

The API does return those statuses. An invalid PAT against
`GET /v1/projects/{ref}/branches` — whose only documented failure is `500` —
returns a `401` with a structured body:

```console
$ curl -s -w '\nstatus=%{http_code}\n' \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer sbp_invalid' \
    https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/abcdefghijklmnopqrst/branches
{"message":"JWT could not be decoded"}
status=401
```

So a reader of https://supabase.com/docs/reference/api/v1-list-all-branches is told
the only way this call fails is a server error.

### 2. `GET /v1/branches/{id}/diff` requires `environment:write`, and the page doesn't say why

```
GET /v1/branches/{branch_id_or_ref}/diff
  x-oauth-scope:      environment:write
  x-fga-permissions:  [[branching_development_write], [branching_production_write]]
```

This is the **only** `GET` operation in the entire v1 spec whose `x-oauth-scope`
ends in `:write`. The three other branching reads (`GET /v1/branches/{id}`,
`GET /v1/projects/{ref}/branches`, `GET /v1/projects/{ref}/branches/{name}`) all
use `environment:read`.

**I suspect this is deliberate**, and I'd rather name the likely reason than assume
a mistake: `V1DiffABranchParams` exposes a `pgdelta` toggle ("Use pg-delta instead
of Migra for diffing"), and both Migra and pg-delta compute a diff by provisioning a
shadow database and applying schema to it. If the endpoint does that server-side,
`:write` is the correct scope and the read/write split is working as designed.

Either way the docs don't say. An integrator building a read-only branch dashboard
reads the page, sees a `GET`, and has to request `environment:write` — which also
grants branch delete, reset, merge and push. Their end user's consent screen then
says the app can destroy branches, with no explanation available anywhere.
(Related appetite for finer-grained read scopes in #49702.)

## Describe the improvement

1. Add `401` / `403` / `429` to the 11 branching operations that omit them, matching
   `DELETE /v1/projects/{ref}/branches` and the other 151 operations in v1.
2. On `v1-diff-a-branch`, state why the scope is `environment:write` — or, if the
   scope is wider than the operation needs, narrow it to `environment:read`.

## Additional context

These pages are generated from the OpenAPI spec, which is also consumed for code
generation — including `packages/api`, the typed Management API client in the CLI
TypeScript rewrite. So the gap isn't only prose: generated clients model branching
failures as "`500` or a transport error", and a `401` from an expired PAT surfaces
as an unexpected response rather than an auth failure the caller can branch on.

Reproduction against the live spec:

```bash
curl -s https://api.supabase.com/api/v1-json -o spec.json
```

```python
import json
spec = json.load(open("spec.json"))
M = ("get", "post", "put", "patch", "delete")

# (1) error responses documented per branching operation
for path, item in sorted(spec["paths"].items()):
    if "branch" not in path:
        continue
    for method, op in item.items():
        if method in M:
            errs = sorted(c for c in op.get("responses", {}) if c[0] in "45")
            print(f"{method.upper():7}{path:44}{errs}")

# (2) the only GET in v1 requiring a :write scope
for path, item in spec["paths"].items():
    op = item.get("get")
    if op and str(op.get("x-oauth-scope", "")).endswith(":write"):
        print(path, "->", op["x-oauth-scope"])
```

Spec checked 2026-09-08: OpenAPI 3.0.0, 115 paths / 169 operations / 147 schemas.

One broader thing I left out because it isn't specific to branching: 580 of the 586
documented `4xx`/`5xx` responses across v1 carry no schema at all, so the
`{"message": ...}` body above isn't modelled anywhere and generated clients type
every error body as unknown. Happy to open that separately if it's usefull!

I'd be glad to open a PR for the response-documentation half if the spec is
generated from decorators in a repo that accepts external contributions, a pointer
would be welcome, since the generating source doesn't appear to be public.
qualityReasoning: Detailed issue description (5735 chars) with technical context, code/log references, and clear scope.

title: Provide a Portainer Stack for Supabase Deployment
body:
## Link 

[Self-Hosting with Docker](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/self-hosting/docker)

## Describe the problem

The current documentation provides guidance on self-hosting Supabase using Docker, but it lacks specific instructions for deploying Supabase using Portainer stacks. Portainer is a widely used tool that simplifies Docker container management through a user-friendly GUI. Many users rely on Portainer to deploy and manage their Docker environments.

The ambiguity arises because there are nuances and additional steps required when deploying Supabase with Portainer compared to standard Docker Compose. For instance, handling environment variables, managing secrets, and configuring services may differ in Portainer. This can lead to confusion and misconfiguration for users attempting to deploy Supabase using Portainer stacks based solely on the existing Docker documentation.

## Describe the improvement

I recommend adding a dedicated section or guide in the documentation that covers deploying Supabase using Portainer stacks. This should include:

- **A complete `docker-compose.yml` file** compatible with Portainer, ensuring all functionalities are included without omissions or truncations.
- **Detailed instructions on setting environment variables** within Portainer's GUI, highlighting any differences from standard Docker Compose setups.
- **Notes on specific configurations or considerations** when using Portainer, such as managing secrets securely and handling port mappings.
- **Clarification on any differences** between the standard Docker setup and Portainer deployment to eliminate ambiguity and assist users in a smooth setup process.

By providing Portainer-specific guidance, the documentation would greatly assist users who utilize Portainer for managing their Docker deployments, reducing potential setup issues and improving the overall user experience.

## Additional context

I recently worked on deploying Supabase using Portainer and compiled a working `docker-compose.yml` file and corresponding environment variables tailored for Portainer. Including such examples in the documentation could serve as a helpful reference for other users.

### **docker-compose.yml**

```yaml
version: '3.8'

services:
  db:
    image: supabase/postgres:15.2.0
    container_name: supabase-db
    restart: always
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB}
      POSTGRES_PORT: ${POSTGRES_PORT}
    volumes:
      - db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    ports:
      - "${POSTGRES_PORT}:${POSTGRES_PORT}"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  supavisor:
    image: supabase/supavisor:latest
    container_name: supabase-supavisor
    restart: always
    environment:
      PORT: ${SUPAVISOR_PORT}
      DATABASE_URL: "postgres://${POSTGRES_USER}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db:${POSTGRES_PORT}/${POSTGRES_DB}"
      JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET}
    depends_on:
      - db
    ports:
      - "${SUPAVISOR_PORT}:${SUPAVISOR_PORT}"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--spider", "http://localhost:${SUPAVISOR_PORT}/health"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  kong:
```

### **Environment Variables**

```dotenv
# Database configuration
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=your_postgres_password
POSTGRES_USER=postgres
POSTGRES_DB=postgres
POSTGRES_PORT=5432

# Supavisor configuration
SUPAVISOR_PORT=6543

# Kong ports
KONG_HTTP_PORT=8000
KONG_HTTPS_PORT=8443

# JWT Secret (must be a long, secure random string)
JWT_SECRET=your_jwt_secret

# Supabase API keys (generate using your JWT_SECRET)
ANON_KEY=your_anon_key
SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=your_service_role_key

# Dashboard credentials
DASHBOARD_USERNAME=supabase
DASHBOARD_PASSWORD=your_dashboard_password

# Site URL
SITE_URL=http://your-site-url.com

# Studio port
STUDIO_PORT=8080

# SMTP settings (for sending emails)
SMTP_HOST=your_smtp_host
SMTP_PORT=587
SMTP_USER=your_smtp_user
SMTP_PASS=your_smtp_password
SMTP_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@example.com
```

### **Instructions**

#### **1. Replace Placeholder Values**

Before deploying, **replace all placeholder values** with your own secure values:

- **`your_postgres_password`**: A strong password for the Postgres database.
- **`your_jwt_secret`**: A secure, random string (at least 32 characters).
- **`your_anon_key`** and **`your_service_role_key`**: JWT tokens generated using your `JWT_SECRET`.
- **`your_dashboard_password`**: A strong password for accessing Supabase Studio.
- **`http://your-site-url.com`**: Replace with the actual URL where your Supabase instance will be accessible.
- **SMTP settings**: Set these variables with your SMTP server details to enable email functionality.

#### **2. Generate the `ANON_KEY` and `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`**

To generate these keys:

- **Use a JWT generation tool**: You can use [jwt.io](https://jwt.io/) or a command-line tool like `openssl`.
- **For the `ANON_KEY`**:
  - **Header**: `{"alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT"}`
  - **Payload**: `{"role": "anon"}`
  - **Secret**: Your `JWT_SECRET`
- **For the `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`**:
  - **Header**: `{"alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT"}`
  - **Payload**: `{"role": "service_role"}`
  - **Secret**: Your `JWT_SECRET`
- **Copy the tokens**: Use the generated tokens as the values for `ANON_KEY` and `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`.

#### **3. Deploy the Stack in Portainer**

- **Open Portainer** and navigate to **Stacks**.
- Click **Add stack**.
- **Name your stack** (e.g., `supabase`).
- **Copy and paste** the `docker-compose.yml` content into the **Web editor**.
- **Scroll down** to the **Environment variables** section.
  - **Switch to advanced mode** to paste all variables at once.
  - **Paste** the environment variables list provided above.
  - **Ensure** all placeholder values have been replaced with your own.
- Click **Deploy the stack**.

#### **4. Access Supabase Studio**

- Navigate to `http://<your-server-ip>:${STUDIO_PORT}` (default is `8080`).
- Log in using the `DASHBOARD_USERNAME` and `DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` you set in the environment variables.

---

Including Portainer-specific instructions and configurations like the above in the official documentation would greatly help users who prefer or rely on Portainer for managing their Docker containers. It would eliminate ambiguity and provide a clear pathway for deploying Supabase in a Portainer environment.

title: Using supabase breaks vitest due to improper ESM handling by @supabase/node-fetch
body:
# Bug report

<!-- 

⚠️ We receive a lot of bug reports which have already been solved or discussed. If you are looking for help, please try these first:

- Docs: https://docs.supabase.com
- Discussions: https://github.com/supabase/supabase/discussions
- Discord: https://discord.supabase.com

Before opening a bug report, please verify the following: 

-->

- [x] I confirm this is a bug with Supabase, not with my own application. 
- [x] I confirm I have searched the [Docs](https://docs.supabase.com), GitHub [Discussions](https://github.com/supabase/supabase/discussions), and [Discord](https://discord.supabase.com). 

## Describe the bug

Using supabase breaks vitest due to improper ESM handling by @supabase/node-fetch
Related to: https://github.com/supabase/supabase/issues/21261

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior, please provide code snippets or a repository:

1. Create typescript project with vitest and supabase
2. Import supabase somewhere and run a test, see the following:
```
 FAIL  test/entry-date.spec.ts [ test/entry-date.spec.ts ]
Error: No such module "Users/bob/notes/node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+postgrest-js@1.16.3/node_modules/@supabase/postgrest-js/dist/cjs/@supabase/node-fetch".
 ❯ Users/bob/notes/node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+postgrest-js@1.16.3/node_modules/@supabase/postgrest-js/dist/cjs/PostgrestBuilder.js?mf_vitest_no_cjs_esm_shim:7:38
 ❯ Users/bob/notes/node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+postgrest-js@1.16.3/node_modules/@supabase/postgrest-js/dist/cjs/PostgrestTransformBuilder.js?mf_vitest_no_cjs_esm_shim:6:44
 ❯ Users/bob/notes/node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+postgrest-js@1.16.3/node_modules/@supabase/postgrest-js/dist/cjs/PostgrestFilterBuilder.js?mf_vitest_no_cjs_esm_shim:6:53
 ❯ Users/bob/notes/node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+postgrest-js@1.16.3/node_modules/@supabase/postgrest-js/dist/cjs/PostgrestQueryBuilder.js?mf_vitest_no_cjs_esm_shim:6:50
 ❯ Users/bob/notes/node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+postgrest-js@1.16.3/node_modules/@supabase/postgrest-js/dist/cjs/PostgrestClient.js?mf_vitest_no_cjs_esm_shim:6:49
 ❯ Users/bob/notes/node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+postgrest-js@1.16.3/node_modules/@supabase/postgrest-js/dist/cjs/index.js?mf_vitest_no_cjs_esm_shim:8:43
```
3. Remove the supabase library and install another few dozen libraries
4. Notice that the problem only happens when the supabase library is installed.

## Expected behavior

The supabase library does not cause tests to break.

## System information

- OS: macOS
- Version of supabase-js: Latest (2.45.6)
- Version of Node.js: 20.15.0

## Additional context

In February, @kjhughes already analyzed where the problem lies, but he did not receive any replies.

> * For the browser target, `node-fetch` should not even be needed because browsers have native `fetch` support.
> * Every `@supabase/*` package has the following `package.json` properties:
> 
> ```
>   "main": "dist/main/index.js",
>   "module": "dist/module/index.js",
> ```
> 
> * _**...except**_ `@supabase/node-fetch`, which is noted in the error message as failing to import in `PostgrestBuilder.js:1:8`.
> 
> The above suggests that Supabase is perhaps not robustly handling its `fetch()` needs for ESM modules in the browser, either because it ought to be using the browser-native `fetch()` rather than `node-fetch` or because `@supabase/node-fetch` is not configured in the manner of all other `@supabase/*` packages wrt the above noted `package.json` properties.

title: [Bug]: Draft orders never discover the first eligible automatic promotion
body:
## Bug report

### Package information

Relevant packages:

```json
{
  "@medusajs/medusa": "2.21.0",
  "@medusajs/core-flows": "2.21.0",
  "@medusajs/promotion": "2.21.0"
}
```

- Node.js: v24.16.0
- Database: PostgreSQL 17
- Operating system: Windows
- Browser: Chromium (relevant only to the POS use case; the defect is in backend core flows)

### What happened?

An eligible automatic promotion is never discovered when a Draft Order first becomes eligible during an edit.

In v2.21.0, both `addDraftOrderItemsWorkflow` and `updateDraftOrderItemWorkflow` derive codes from `order.promotions` and only invoke `computeDraftOrderAdjustmentsWorkflow` when that list is already non-empty. `computeDraftOrderAdjustmentsWorkflow` has the same gate: when `order.promotions` is empty, it writes empty replacement adjustments; it only calls `getActionsToComputeFromPromotionsStep` when at least one promotion is already attached.

That prevents the Promotion Module from performing the first evaluation that would discover an `is_automatic` promotion. The Promotion Module's `computeActions([], context)` path does support querying automatic promotions, but the Draft Order workflows never reach it when the order starts with no promotions.

Manually adding the same promotion through `addDraftOrderPromotionWorkflow` first attaches its code and then computes adjustments. The discount therefore works when entered manually, and subsequent item mutations can refresh it, but it does not apply automatically when the Draft Order first meets the promotion conditions.

The gate is promotion-type agnostic, so this affects native automatic promotion types as well as custom promotion types.

For POS use cases, like the one I am working on, this means that the behavior a clerk would expect in a POS - promotions automatically recording and adjusting prices as they scan items to the cart - doesn't happen. And clerks are sad.

Relevant v2.21.0 source:

- [`addDraftOrderItemsWorkflow`](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/blob/v2.21.0/packages/core/core-flows/src/draft-order/workflows/add-draft-order-items.ts)
- [`updateDraftOrderItemWorkflow`](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/blob/v2.21.0/packages/core/core-flows/src/draft-order/workflows/update-draft-order-item.ts)
- [`computeDraftOrderAdjustmentsWorkflow`](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/blob/v2.21.0/packages/core/core-flows/src/draft-order/workflows/compute-draft-order-adjustments.ts)
- [`PromotionModuleService.computeActions`](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/blob/v2.21.0/packages/modules/promotion/src/services/promotion-module.ts)

### Expected behavior

When items are added to a Draft Order or their quantities change, active automatic promotions should be evaluated even when no promotion is already attached. Eligible automatic promotions should be reflected in adjustments and the Draft Order's promotions, then recalculated or removed when later mutations change eligibility.

This is especially important for POS integrations that use a Draft Order as the clerk's live register cart. As products are scanned, the clerk should see every qualifying automatic promotion without entering a code. A clerk cannot safely be expected to memorize every active store promotion, and silently missing one can overcharge the customer.

### Actual behavior

No automatic promotion computation occurs while `order.promotions` is empty. The Draft Order remains undiscounted after it becomes eligible. Manually adding the promotion code seeds `order.promotions`, after which the same promotion computes correctly.

Store carts do not have this problem: their refresh path invokes `updateCartPromotionsWorkflow` even when the explicit code list is empty, allowing automatic promotions to be discovered.

### Steps to reproduce

Using a vanilla Medusa v2.21.0 application:

1. Create and activate a native automatic promotion, such as 10% off products in a selected collection.
2. Create a Draft Order without applying any promotion.
3. Begin a Draft Order edit.
4. Add a product that satisfies the automatic promotion, or update its quantity so the conditions are met.
5. Confirm or preview the edit.
6. Observe that no automatic promotion or adjustment has been added.
7. Begin another edit and add the same promotion explicitly with `addDraftOrderPromotionWorkflow`.
8. Observe that the promotion now computes and the discount is applied.

### Reproduction repository

The issue reproduces directly in the tagged upstream implementation without application-specific code:

https://github.com/medusajs/medusa/tree/v2.21.0

The source links above identify the type-agnostic conditions that prevent the first automatic-promotion computation.

### Suggested direction

Draft Order cart mutations should perform full automatic-promotion reconciliation: discover newly eligible automatic promotions, attach and calculate them, recalculate existing ones, and remove those that are no longer eligible. If automatic promotions are intentionally limited to Store carts, that limitation should be documented and a supported reconciliation workflow should be provided for POS/Draft Order integrations.

title: Payment webhook: `/hooks/payment/pp_<id>` acks 200 then fails with `pp_pp_…`; MCP provider guide recommends that form
body:
**Medusa version:** `@medusajs/*` 2.21.0, Node 22, self-hosted (Postgres + `event-bus-redis`)

#### What happens

The Medusa MCP server's `get_payment_provider_integration_guide` tells you to point a custom provider's webhooks at the **full** provider id:

> `:provider` must be the **full registered provider id** — `pp_{identifier}_{id}`, e.g. `pp_myprovider_myprovider` — **not** the bare `static identifier` … This is the single most common webhook misconfiguration

That URL fails every time. `PaymentModuleService.getWebhookActionAndData` adds the prefix itself (`@medusajs/payment`, `dist/services/payment-module.js`):

```js
async getWebhookActionAndData(eventData, sharedContext) {
    const providerId = `pp_${eventData.provider}`;
    return await this.paymentProviderService_.getWebhookActionAndData(providerId, eventData.payload);
}
```

So `/hooks/payment/pp_pagbank_pagbank` resolves `pp_pp_pagbank_pagbank`:

```
POST /hooks/payment/pp_pagbank_pagbank ← - (200)
Processing payment.webhook_received (priority: 100) which has 1 subscribers
AwilixResolutionError: Could not resolve 'pp_pp_pagbank_pagbank'.
Unable to retrieve the payment provider with id: pp_pp_pagbank_pagbank
One or more subscribers of payment.webhook_received failed. Retrying...
```

After three retries the event is dropped. **The failure is silent from the payment provider's side.** The route answers `200` before the subscriber runs, so the provider's dashboard shows every delivery as successful while no payment is ever updated. For async methods such as PIX, boleto or OXXO, orders stay `awaiting` forever.

The official docs are correct. The [Stripe provider page](https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/commerce-modules/payment/payment-provider/stripe#setup-stripe-webhooks) says "without the `pp_` prefix", and [Payment Webhook Events](https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/commerce-modules/payment/webhook-events) documents `/hooks/payment/[identifier]_[provider]`. Only the MCP guide contradicts them, and it does so emphatically, which is how we ended up here.

#### Steps to reproduce

1. Build a payment module provider with `static identifier = "myprovider"` and register it in `medusa-config.ts` with `id: "myprovider"`. Its provider id is `pp_myprovider_myprovider`.
2. Implement `getWebhookActionAndData` to return any action.
3. Run `curl -X POST localhost:9000/hooks/payment/pp_myprovider_myprovider -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'`. The response is `200 OK`.
4. Wait about 5 seconds for the delayed event. The server log shows `AwilixResolutionError: Could not resolve 'pp_pp_myprovider_myprovider'`, retried and then dropped.
5. Send the same request to `/hooks/payment/myprovider_myprovider`. The provider's `getWebhookActionAndData` is called.

#### Expected behaviour

Any one of these would have prevented it:

1. **Fix the MCP guide.** Its `<webhook_route>` section and `success_criteria` should say `/hooks/payment/{identifier}_{id}`, with no `pp_`, matching the docs.
2. **Accept both forms.** If `:provider` already starts with `pp_`, don't prefix it again. The mistake is easy to make, since `pp_…` is the id you see everywhere else (the region's providers, `/store/payment-providers`, the `payment` table).
3. **Fail loudly.** Resolve the provider before acknowledging and answer `404` when it isn't registered, or at least log a hint such as "provider id already carries the pp_ prefix". This overlaps with #16252 (closed as stale), which asked for route-level rejection of unregistered providers for security-scanner reasons. This is a second, functional reason for the same guard.

#### Workaround

Use `/hooks/payment/{identifier}_{id}` (for example `/hooks/payment/pagbank_pagbank`).

title: Store cart accepts fractional line-item quantity: 0.1 is stored as 0 and makes the cart uncompletable
body:
The store cart line-items endpoint validates quantity with z.number().gt(0) but not .int(), so a
fractional quantity passes validation and is coerced on store. 0.1 becomes quantity 0, which the
completion step then refuses, so the cart can never be paid for. 1.5 becomes 2, so a shopper who
asks for 1.5 is charged for two.

Medusa 2.20.1, stock starter, Postgres.

Steps:
1. POST /store/carts with a region_id (publishable key header set).
2. POST /store/carts/{id}/line-items with {"variant_id":"<variant>","quantity":0.1}
3. Returns 200. GET /store/carts/{id} shows the line item at quantity 0, item_total 0.
4. POST /store/carts/{id}/complete fails, and the item cannot be raised off 0.

I expected quantity to be validated as an integer, the same way the endpoint already rejects 0
and -1. A quantity the cart accepts should be one checkout can take.

Same endpoint, other values: 0.5 -> 1, 1.2 -> 1, 1.5 -> 2, 2.7 -> 3. The string "3" is rejected.
So the guard catches the wrong shapes but not fractions.

In 2.20.1 the store carts validators define line-item quantity as z.number().gt(0). Adding .int()
would close it.

This is the same class as #13363, which was closed as completed, but it still reproduces on 2.20.1.

title: [Bug]: Cloud storefront build runs `pnpm add --save`, which pnpm 12 rejects, so opennextjs-cloudflare is never installed
body:
## System information

### Package.json file (workspace root, as it was when the build failed)

```json
{
  "name": "teepham-medical-b2b-portal-1",
  "private": false,
  "packageManager": "pnpm@12.5.1",
  "engines": {

  },
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "turbo dev",
    "build": "turbo build",
    "start": "turbo start",
    "lint": "turbo lint",
    "test": "turbo test"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@medusajs/eslint-plugin": "2.21.0",
    "ajv": "^8.13.0",
    "cheerio": "^1.2.0",
    "eslint": "^9.39.4",
    "jiti": "^2.7.0",
    "prettier": "^3.2.5",
    "turbo": "^2.0.14",
    "turndown": "^7.2.4"
  }
}
```

Turborepo workspace: `apps/backend` (`@medusajs/medusa` 2.21.0) and `apps/storefront` (Next.js 15.5.25). The failure is in Medusa Cloud's build, so the relevant code is `@repo/build-detector`'s `frontend-runner.js` as bundled in `@medusajs/mcloud` 0.1.13.

### Node.js version

Cloud's storefront image: `node:24.15.0-slim`. Locally: v24.21.0.

### Database and its version

Not involved (Cloud-provisioned PostgreSQL; the failure is at build time).

### Operating system name and version

Cloud's Linux build image; reproduced locally on macOS 26.6.2 with `mcloud local build --type storefront` and in a plain `node:24.15.0-slim` container.

### Browser name

Not applicable.

## Describe the issue

### What happened?

The Medusa Cloud storefront build fails for a monorepo whose `packageManager` is pnpm 12. The generated `build-fe.sh` (from `generateBuildScripts` in `frontend-runner.js`) installs the Cloudflare adapter into the storefront with:

```sh
cd <repo>/apps/storefront && pnpm add --save-dev wrangler@4.86.0 && pnpm add --save @opennextjs/cloudflare@1.19.8 && cd -
pnpm approve-builds workerd
```

pnpm 12 (the Rust port; 12.5.1 is the current `latest`) rejects `--save`:

```
error: unexpected argument '--save' found

  tip: a similar argument exists: '--save-dev'

Usage: pnpm add --save-dev <PACKAGE_NAMES>...
```

Its production flag is `--save-prod` / `-P`, which pnpm 10 and 11 accept as well. Because `build-fe.sh` has no `set -e`, the script carries on: `.env` is written, `next build` succeeds, and the build only dies at the last line:

```
./build-fe.sh: 12: /app/workdir/<repo>/node_modules/.bin/opennextjs-cloudflare: not found
```

The backend build of the same commit succeeds, so the deployment ends as Backend `deployed`, Storefront `build-failed`.

A second, related problem hits pnpm 11 as well as 12: the `pnpm add --save-dev wrangler` line runs before the runner's own `pnpm approve-builds workerd`, and with pnpm 11+'s default `strictDepBuilds` that add fails with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` (`Ignored build scripts: workerd@1.20260426.1`) unless the customer already has `workerd` listed in `allowBuilds` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. pnpm also writes a placeholder line `workerd: set this to true or false` into the workspace file at that point. The approve step exists to handle exactly this, but it runs too late to help.

### Expected behavior

A workspace pinned to any pnpm major that Cloud's Node images can run (10, 11, 12) builds the storefront without repo-side workarounds, or the prerequisites docs state which pnpm majors the storefront build supports.

Suggested fix in `generateBuildScripts` for `packageManager.type === "pnpm"`:

- `addProdDependencyCommand = "pnpm add --save-prod"` (works on 10, 11 and 12);
- run `pnpm approve-builds workerd` before the adds, or otherwise record the workerd decision up front, so `strictDepBuilds` does not fail the wrangler add.

### Actual behavior

On pnpm 12.5.1: `pnpm add --save-dev wrangler` fails on `workerd` under `strictDepBuilds` unless `workerd` is pre-allowed; with it pre-allowed, `pnpm add --save @opennextjs/cloudflare` fails with the `--save` parse error, the adapter is never installed, and the build ends with `opennextjs-cloudflare: not found`.

On pnpm 11.26.0 with `workerd: true` in `allowBuilds`: both adds succeed, `pnpm approve-builds workerd` prints `[WARN] The following packages are not awaiting approval: workerd`, and the build completes. Without the `allowBuilds` entry the wrangler add fails as above.

Cloud deployments, if useful for the Cloud team: `build_01M2YB9TYDFRN5WCCCGZ0VTXH4` is the pnpm 12 failure; `build_01M2YH9K3QRMQD1YBHNZGF8NSJ` is the same repository passing after moving to pnpm 11.26.0 with `workerd: true`.

## Reproduction

### Link to reproduction repo

The affected repository is private. The bug is independent of its contents: any Turborepo workspace with `"packageManager": "pnpm@12.5.1"` and a Next.js storefront reproduces it, and `mcloud local build --type storefront` (which runs the same generated script in Cloud's image) shows the exact failure. The parser rejection alone can be seen anywhere:

```sh
mkdir t && cd t && npm init -y >/dev/null
corepack pnpm@12.5.1 add --save is-odd@3.0.1     # error: unexpected argument '--save' found
corepack pnpm@11.26.0 add --save is-odd@3.0.1    # works
corepack pnpm@12.5.1 add --save-prod is-odd@3.0.1  # works
```

I can put together a minimal public repository if that helps triage.

title: [Bug]: Filtering orders by most order_item fields (e.g. items.fulfilled_quantity) throws 'not existing property OrderLineItem'
body:
## Bug Report

### Description

Filtering orders by fields that live on the order_item join entity fails for every field except the three that are handled in a special-case list. For example, listOrders with a filter on items.fulfilled_quantity errors with:

Trying to query by not existing property OrderLineItem.fulfilled_quantity

### Root cause

In packages/modules/order/src/utils/transform-order.ts, mapRepositoryToOrderModel remaps filters under where.items into the repository shape. The public order model exposes items as the order_item join entity (whose columns include quantity, fulfilled_quantity, shipped_quantity, delivered_quantity, return_requested_quantity, return_received_quantity, return_dismissed_quantity, written_off_quantity), while the line item itself lives under items.item.

The remap keeps only quantity, unit_price, and compare_at_unit_price on the join entity and routes everything else under item. Since order_line_item has no column named fulfilled_quantity (or any of the other join-entity fields), the metadata validation fails and the query throws.

Reproducible directly against the order module:

const _ = await service.listOrders({
  items: { fulfilled_quantity: 0 },
})

### Expected behavior

All fields that exist on the order_item join entity can be used in items.<field> filters, the same way quantity already works: the filter resolves against the join entity and the query succeeds.

### Actual behavior

The query throws Trying to query by not existing property OrderLineItem.<field> for every join-entity field other than quantity, unit_price, compare_at_unit_price.

### Medusa version
2.19.x (develop @ 847612908f)

I have a fix and tests ready that route the full join-entity field set (and the price fields, consistent with the existing quantity handling) to the order_item entity, covering both unit and live-database integration paths.

title: Fulfillment providers cannot read variant data through the admin fulfillment flow (create-fulfillment omits items.variant.metadata)
body:
## Summary

A fulfillment provider that needs per-line variant data — any print-on-demand or dropship integration, which is most non-manual providers — cannot get it through the admin fulfillment flow.

`createOrderFulfillmentWorkflow` hydrates the order from a fixed field list that omits `items.variant.metadata`, and the `items` argument handed to the provider is a list of persisted `fulfillment_item` rows — a model with no `variant` relation and no `variant_id`. The result: `provider.createFulfillment` receives no way to map an order line onto a vendor SKU.

Version: `@medusajs/core-flows` / `@medusajs/fulfillment` **2.19.0**

## What we hit

First real order through the admin flow, `POST /admin/orders/:id/fulfillments`, against a custom print-on-demand provider that reads `item.variant?.metadata` (the natural reading of the `createFulfillment(data, items, order, fulfillment)` signature):

```
400 invalid_data
Variant undefined is not mappable to a vendor SKU
```

`item.variant_id` was `undefined` — not merely `item.variant.metadata`. Every unit test passed, because fixtures construct hydrated items; the real caller never produces them.

## Root cause, traced through 2.19.0

1. **`create-fulfillment.ts` — the order query omits variant metadata.** `useQueryGraphStep` requests `items.variant.manage_inventory`, `items.variant.sku`, `items.variant.weight`, `items.variant.hs_code`, `items.variant.origin_country` … but never `items.variant.metadata`.
2. **`prepareFulfillmentData` flattens the lines.** Each order item becomes `{ line_item_id, inventory_item_id, quantity, title, sku, barcode }`. Anything else on the variant is dropped here regardless of what step 1 fetched.
3. **`fulfillment_item` cannot store it.** The model (`@medusajs/fulfillment/models/fulfillment-item`) is `{ id, title, sku, barcode, quantity, line_item_id, inventory_item_id, fulfillment }`. No `variant`, no `variant_id`.
4. **The provider receives those rows verbatim** from `FulfillmentModuleService.createFulfillment`.

A provider cannot resolve the data for itself either: its container is the fulfillment module's, not the app's. Enumerated at runtime on 2.19.0 it holds the module's own repositories/services plus `logger`, `manager`, `configModule`, `event_bus`, `caching`, `__pg_connection__` — no `query`, no `remoteQuery`, no `product`.

## Proposed fix — one line, plus one docs paragraph

The `order` argument **is** passed to the provider untouched (`prepareFulfillmentData` returns `order: order`; the module service forwards it). So adding the field to the query list makes variant metadata reachable:

```diff
--- a/packages/core/core-flows/src/order/workflows/create-fulfillment.ts
+++ b/packages/core/core-flows/src/order/workflows/create-fulfillment.ts
@@ fields: [
       "items.variant.material",
+      "items.variant.metadata",
       "items.variant_title",
```

Verified against a live 2.19.0 instance — same order, same query engine:

| field list | `items[0].variant` keys | `variant.metadata` |
|---|---|---|
| today | `manage_inventory, sku, weight, hs_code, id` | **absent** |
| with the patch | `manage_inventory, sku, weight, hs_code, metadata, id` | present |

**What the one-liner does not fix:** it puts metadata on `order.items[].variant.metadata`, not on the `items` argument — `fulfillment_item` still cannot carry a variant. A provider must correlate `items[].line_item_id → order.items[].id` and read the variant from the order. That is not obvious from the signature, and the provider guide should say it outright. Suggested addition:

> The `items` argument is a list of `fulfillment_item` records. It carries `line_item_id`, `quantity`, `title`, `sku` and `barcode` only — it has no variant relation. To read variant data (including `metadata`), match `item.line_item_id` against `order.items[].id` and read the variant from the order.

Happy to open the PR for the one-line change plus the docs paragraph — it's ready to go.

Two smaller observations from the same debugging session (unserialized entities handed to providers, and `additional_data` being the only documented-nowhere channel that survives the path) in a comment below, kept out of the main report so it stays single-purpose.

title: Fulfillment providers receive unserialized entities — non-enumerable bigNumber quantity is silently lost by any copy, sending wrong values to vendor APIs
body:
## Summary

`FulfillmentModuleService.createFulfillment` serializes its return value for its caller, but invokes the provider with the raw, unserialized entities. On those entities the bigNumber `quantity` is a non-enumerable accessor: `typeof item.quantity === "number"`, while `Object.keys(item)` lists only `raw_quantity`. Any provider that copies an item — `{ ...item }`, `Object.assign`, `structuredClone` — silently loses the quantity.

Version: `@medusajs/fulfillment` **2.19.0**. Found in the same debugging session as #16621; split out per single-purpose reporting.

## What we hit

Our print-on-demand provider built its vendor payload by spreading the item. The vendor API answered:

```
items[0].copies: MustBeGreaterThan 0, providedValue 0
```

A wrong value reached a third party — no crash, no error anywhere on the Medusa side. A vendor that accepted or defaulted the field would have shipped the wrong quantity.

## Root cause

- `createFulfillment` returns `await this.baseRepository_.serialize(fulfillment)` to its caller, but `provider.createFulfillment(data, items, order, fulfillment)` receives the entity items unserialized.
- bigNumber fields are accessor-based: enumerable `raw_quantity`, non-enumerable `quantity`. Direct property reads work, so the bug is invisible until the first copy — and building an outbound payload by copying is exactly what a provider does.

## Proposed fix

Serialize the entities before the provider call — matching what the module service already does for its own caller — or, failing that, document the shape so provider authors know spreads are unsafe. Serialization is the safer default: the values cross a process boundary to third-party APIs from here.

Happy to open a PR for the serialize-before-provider-call change if maintainers prefer that direction.

(Observation 2 from the #16621 comment — `additional_data` being the only undocumented channel that survives the path — stays folded into #16621's docs suggestion rather than becoming its own report.)

### Expected behavior

Either the config loader supports the TS7 toolchain, or Medusa declares the supported TypeScript range so users don't discover this at build time.

title: Adding a value to an existing product option does not link it to the product (silently invisible in admin)
body:
### Package.json file

```json
{
  "@medusajs/admin-sdk": "2.17.2",
  "@medusajs/cli": "2.17.2",
  "@medusajs/framework": "2.17.2",
  "@medusajs/medusa": "2.17.2",
  "@medusajs/test-utils": "2.17.2"
}
```

Also verified against **2.21.0** — see "Root cause" below; the affected code is byte-identical, so upgrading does not fix it.

### Node.js version

20

### Database and its version

PostgreSQL 18.6

### Operating system name and version

Linux (Docker, Railway) — also reproduced against the same database from macOS 15

### Browser name

Chrome 152

### What happended?

Adding a value to an **existing** product option silently does nothing visible. The value row is created in `product_option_value`, but no row is created in `product_product_option_value`, so the value is never linked to the product.

Consequences:

- the new value does **not** appear in the "Type" dropdown when creating or editing a variant, so no variant can ever use it;
- it does not appear in the product's option value list either;
- `GET /admin/products/:id?fields=options.values.value` does not return it, because the product graph resolves option values through the link table;
- there is **no error** — the save request succeeds, the admin shows no message, and a page reload changes nothing.

Values created **together with the option** are fine — those go through `addProductOptionToProduct_`, which does write the link rows.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Create a product with one option `Type` and one value `A`.
2. Edit the product and add value `B` to the existing `Type` option. Save.
3. Reload the product page and open "Create variant".
4. Only `A` is selectable. `B` is nowhere in the UI.
5. In the database:

```sql
SELECT pov.value,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM product_product_option_value ppov
                WHERE ppov.product_option_value_id = pov.id
                  AND ppov.deleted_at IS NULL) AS linked
FROM product_option_value pov
JOIN product_option po ON po.id = pov.option_id
WHERE po.id = '<option id>' AND pov.deleted_at IS NULL;
```

`A` → `linked = true`, `B` → `linked = false`.

The same asymmetry is visible through the Query API: `query.graph({ entity: "product_option_value", filters: { option_id: [...] } })` returns both values, while `query.graph({ entity: "product", fields: ["options.values.value"] })` returns only the linked one.

### Expected behavior

Adding a value to an existing product option links it to the product, so it can be selected when creating a variant — the same result as creating the option with both values at once.

### Actual behavior

The value is created but never linked. It is invisible in the admin and in the product graph, permanently and without any error.

### Root cause

`product_product_option_value` was introduced in `Migration20251110180907`, with `Migration20251113183352` backfilling "all existing implicit relationships". Link rows are written in exactly two places in `ProductModuleService`:

- `addProductOptionToProduct_` — the "option together with its values" path,
- the `updateProductOptionValuesOnProduct` path.

`updateProductOptions_`, which the admin product edit goes through, ends with:

```js
const { entities: productOptions } = await this.productOptionService_.upsertWithReplace(
  normalizedInput, { relations: ["values"] }, sharedContext
)
return productOptions
```

It upserts the option with its values — creating the `product_option_value` row — and never touches `product_product_option_value`. So a value added to an existing option gets a row without a link.

I compared `@medusajs/product` **2.17.2** and **2.21.0**: this function is unchanged and neither version adds a link-creation call there.

### Impact

This is not theoretical. On our production catalogue we found three such orphaned values on published products, plus 59 more attached to options no longer linked to any product.

The failure mode is worse than "the value is missing", because it is invisible in both directions:

- the operator cannot tell the save failed — there is no error, and the UI looks the same before and after;
- the value cannot be removed through the admin either, precisely because the admin cannot see it. The only way we found to clear one was to link it first (via `setProductProductOptions`) so it becomes visible, then delete it normally;
- our own catalogue consistency checks could not see it either — they all read option values through the product graph, so an orphaned value is invisible to the exact tooling meant to catch it. We had to add a check that queries `product_option_value` directly.

### Link to reproduction repo

No separate repo — the steps above reproduce on a stock Medusa 2.x install, and the root cause is pinpointed in `@medusajs/product` above. Happy to provide a repo if that is needed to triage.
