title: [bug]: Plane (self-hosted, commercial) • silo + backend • Import • Jobs never leave `TRANSFORMING` state
body:
## Summary

On self-hosted Plane (commercial/enterprise), an import **never completes**: the job is stuck at
status `TRANSFORMING` forever, even though the data is fully imported. The state machine that finalizes
a job is also what dequeues the next one, so **one stuck import blocks all subsequent imports**.

Even though the issue was spotted during a Linear import process, the research suggests the import code path is source-agnostic, so GitHub/Jira/etc. imports are affected the same way.

## Environment

- Deployment: self-hosted (Docker / Swarm), commercial/enterprise images.
- Affected versions: **v3.0.0** and **v3.1.4** (current `stable`) confirmed. The defect is present in
  every image inspected: `v3.0.0, v3.0.1, v3.1.0, v3.1.4, v3.1.5-rc1, v3.2.0-rc3, preview`.
- Components involved: `silo` (importer), `backend` (api + celery worker), Postgres.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a Linear import with a valid PAT against a workspace.
2. Run the import.
3. Watch the job in the UI (or `import_jobs` / `import_reports` in Postgres).

## Expected

Job progresses `INITIATED → PULLING → TRANSFORMING → PUSHING → FINISHED`; the UI shows the import as
complete; the next queued import starts.

## Actual

- Issues and modules **are** created in the target project (the load succeeds).
- `import_reports` shows `completed_batch_count == total_batch_count` (e.g. `3/3`) with issue counts
  populated (e.g. `imported=123, errored=45, total=168`).
- `import_jobs.status` stays `TRANSFORMING` indefinitely; the job never finalizes.
- Because finalization never fires, the **next queued import never starts** - the importer queue stalls.

silo logs confirm the data phase completed, then only UI polling remains:

```
[LINEAR][<job>] Finished pushing data to batch 🚀 ------------------- [....]
Message processed in 3000ms
GET /api/jobs?source=LINEAR&workspaceId=... 200   # (repeats; no further work)
```

## Root cause

silo hard-gates the `TRANSFORMED → PUSHING` transition on a report field the backend never exposes.

**silo** - `apps/silo/dist/start.mjs`, `BaseDataMigrator.update()`:

```js
case "TRANSFORMED":
  if (report.transformed_batch_count != null && report.total_batch_count != null) {
    if (report.transformed_batch_count + 1 === report.total_batch_count) {
      // -> status "PUSHING"
    } else {
      // -> increment transformed_batch_count
    }
  }
```

**backend** - the `ImportReport` model (`plane/ee/models/job.py`) defines only `total_batch_count`,
`completed_batch_count`, `total_issue_count`, `imported_issue_count`, `errored_issue_count`. There is
**no `transformed_batch_count`** field or migration, and `ImportReportCountIncrementAPIView`
(`plane/silo/views/importer_report.py`) never increments it. The API serializer
`ImportReportAPISerializer` (`plane/silo/serializers/job.py`) is a `ModelSerializer` with
`fields = "__all__"`, so it cannot surface a field that doesn't exist on the model.

Therefore the API response has no `transformed_batch_count` key, so in silo
`report.transformed_batch_count` is `undefined`, `undefined != null` is **false**, the whole
`TRANSFORMED` block is skipped, the job never reaches `PUSHING`, and the code that marks the job
finished (and dequeues the next job) is never reached.

Issues still land because the backend's Celery consumer creates them independently of this status
field, which is why the project fills up while the job appears "stuck".

## Impact

- Every import ends in a permanent `TRANSFORMING` state (reads as hung/broken to users).
- The importer queue stalls: no further import can start until the stuck job is cleared manually.

## Workaround (operational, no code change)

After the batches complete, force the job to `FINISHED`, guarded so it only touches jobs whose data
load is genuinely done:

```sql
UPDATE import_jobs
SET status = 'FINISHED', updated_at = now()
WHERE status = 'TRANSFORMING'
  AND report_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM import_reports
    WHERE completed_batch_count >= total_batch_count
      AND total_batch_count > 0
  );
```

Must be repeated for every new import until the defect is fixed.

## Suggested fix

Make the backend provide what silo consumes - on `ImportReport`:

1. Add `transformed_batch_count = models.IntegerField(default=0)` + migration.
2. Increment it in `ImportReportCountIncrementAPIView` alongside the existing counters.

(`ImportReportAPISerializer` needs no change, given `fields = "__all__"`.) With the field present and
incremented, the shipped silo state machine advances to `PUSHING` / `FINISHED` normally.

Alternative: change silo to not depend on `transformed_batch_count` (e.g. gate on
`completed_batch_count` / `total_batch_count`, which the backend already provides).

### Edition
Commercial
### Version
v3.0.0, v3.0.1, v3.1.0, v3.1.4, v3.1.5-rc1, v3.2.0-rc3, preview

title: App sync fails when an app declares a relation to a custom object owned by another app ("has no relation target object metadata")
body:
An app cannot declare a RELATION field whose target is a custom object owned by a **different** app. `twenty apply` fails during "Syncing manifest...", and every later apply of that app fails too. If I create the same relation in the UI it works fine.

The docs ([[extending-objects](https://docs.twenty.com/developers/extend/apps/data/extending-objects)](https://docs.twenty.com/developers/extend/apps/data/extending-objects)) say apps can extend objects of other apps, including relations. Relations to standard objects (person, company, opportunity, task, ...) work fine.

Closest existing thread: #25506 (discussion).

## Version

- Self-hosted Twenty v2.41.0, Docker image `twentycrm/twenty:v2.41.0` (index digest `sha256:47bcefe4e497ceef232f149153a4a61379830f5c898b7da71a5b0e21fd5ea916`, linux/amd64 `sha256:369d52757cf70b64c3f6a54cf424add49863c6fd1f595e5d0030d574859ce9c8`)
- `twenty-sdk` 2.41.0
- Commit: tag `d1bb92d111f91529478da56aa677efbdba230c00`

## Minimal repro

Two new apps, installed on the same workspace. No other code.

**App A** (`xprobe-alpha`): one object, one text field.

```ts
// src/objects/alpha.object.ts
export default defineObject({
  universalIdentifier: 'ba5fad0a-703b-4232-a150-68f22af21ef3',
  nameSingular: 'xprobeAlpha',
  namePlural: 'xprobeAlphas',
  labelSingular: 'XProbe Alpha',
  labelPlural: 'XProbe Alphas',
  icon: 'IconFlask',
  labelIdentifierFieldMetadataUniversalIdentifier: '9199cbf1-5b4c-460f-988f-fc1529c50aba',
  fields: [
    { universalIdentifier: '9199cbf1-5b4c-460f-988f-fc1529c50aba', type: FieldType.TEXT, name: 'name', label: 'Name', icon: 'IconAbc' },
  ],
})
```

**App B** (`xprobe-beta`): the same kind of object (`xprobeBeta`, uid `7c45287c-4ce3-4912-ac6b-24b38cdc6cd8`), plus one relation pair to App A's object.

```ts
// src/fields/beta-alpha.field.ts
export default defineField({
  universalIdentifier: '9af21b9b-cda8-4c23-8d69-d5f4898873fb',
  objectUniversalIdentifier: '7c45287c-4ce3-4912-ac6b-24b38cdc6cd8', // xprobeBeta (own object)
  type: FieldType.RELATION,
  name: 'alpha',
  label: 'Alpha',
  icon: 'IconLink',
  relationTargetObjectMetadataUniversalIdentifier: 'ba5fad0a-703b-4232-a150-68f22af21ef3', // xprobeAlpha (App A)
  relationTargetFieldMetadataUniversalIdentifier: '69d4a091-68d4-43ef-acf2-46171d96373c',
  universalSettings: { relationType: RelationType.MANY_TO_ONE, onDelete: OnDeleteAction.SET_NULL, joinColumnName: 'alphaId' },
})

// src/fields/alpha-betas.field.ts
export default defineField({
  universalIdentifier: '69d4a091-68d4-43ef-acf2-46171d96373c',
  objectUniversalIdentifier: 'ba5fad0a-703b-4232-a150-68f22af21ef3', // xprobeAlpha (App A)
  type: FieldType.RELATION,
  name: 'betas',
  label: 'Betas',
  icon: 'IconLink',
  relationTargetObjectMetadataUniversalIdentifier: '7c45287c-4ce3-4912-ac6b-24b38cdc6cd8',
  relationTargetFieldMetadataUniversalIdentifier: '9af21b9b-cda8-4c23-8d69-d5f4898873fb',
  universalSettings: { relationType: RelationType.ONE_TO_MANY },
})
```

Steps:

1. `twenty apply` App A → OK.
2. `twenty apply` App B → fails:

```
Syncing manifest...
Sync failed with error: Field Metadata of type RELATION or MORPH_RELATION with id <uuid> has no relation target object metadata
```

App A is fully installed before step 2, so this is not an ordering problem.

## What we found

- The field metadata **is** written. The relation works in the workspace GraphQL API (we linked two records and read both sides).
- The same relation created at workspace level (Settings → Data model, same settings) works, and both apps keep syncing.
- An exact copy of that UI-made relation (same relation type, `onDelete`, `isNullable`, icon, join column) declared in app code fails with the same error. So it is not a definition mistake on our side.
- The error is thrown in `object-metadata-with-relations-gql-object-type.generator.ts` (around L117): `flatObjectMetadataMaps` in the app-scoped schema context does not contain the target object, because it is owned by another app.

## Expected

App B syncs, as the docs say. Or, if cross-app relations are not supported, a clear validation error at `plan` time, and a docs update.

## Workaround

Create the relation at workspace level instead of in app code. Both ways work, and both apps keep syncing afterwards:

- UI: Settings → Data model → new Relation field.
- Metadata API: `createOneField` with `relationCreationPayload` (`type`, `targetObjectMetadataId`, `targetFieldLabel`, `targetFieldIcon`).

The fields made this way belong to the workspace custom application, not to either app.

title: MCP: large tool catalogs make agents spend extra calls on discovery
body:
Hey Twenty team!!!! We use a self-hosted Twenty for our CRM and have been testing how well coding agents can use it through MCP.

One recurring problem: agents spend extra calls figuring out which operation to use before getting to the actual CRM work.

Twenty exposes 7 MCP tools, but `get_tool_catalog` returned 215 database operations in our workspace, or 300 operations without a category filter. The coding agent often truncated the response or saved it to a file. Some agents then searched again or read that file to find the operation they needed.

There also seems to be conflicting guidance in the upstream code:

- The [server instructions](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/blob/e893667173c6b1d69099a97239313cf43cc399fb/packages/twenty-server/src/engine/api/mcp/utils/build-mcp-server-instructions.util.ts#L30) tell agents to construct operation names without prior discovery.
- The [catalog description](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/blob/e893667173c6b1d69099a97239313cf43cc399fb/packages/twenty-server/src/engine/core-modules/tool-provider/tools/get-tool-catalog.tool.ts#L39-L40) says they must call it before using `learn_tools` or `execute_tool`.

## What we saw

We completed 140 trials across 6 read-only CRM scenarios using Codex, Claude Code and OpenCode. We collected the calls and responses with an eval system.

```text
Completed trials:               140
Catalog calls in saved traces:   102
Responses truncated or
saved to a file:                 86 of 102
Database catalog:               215 operations
Full catalog:                   300 operations
```

We counted each catalog call once, matching it to its saved response by call ID. Of the 86 responses, 43 had a truncation notice only, 42 had both truncation and a saved-file notice, and one had a saved-file notice only. These figures cover all retained task traces, including partial attempts.

Agents sometimes needed more MCP calls or file reads just to find the right operation. The amount of extra work varied by agent and model.

These runs used self-hosted Twenty over HTTP MCP. The server reported **v2.38.1** on September 22, 2026; we did not record its version during the September 21 runs or rerun on the latest release.

## Suggested direction

Could the instructions make these two paths clear?

- Known object and standard operation: construct the name → `learn_tools` → `execute_tool`.
- Unsure which operation exists: browse the relevant catalog category → `learn_tools` → `execute_tool`.

`learn_tools` should confirm the constructed name exists and provide its arguments. If it doesn't exist, the agent can use discovery. The catalog description could say “use this when you don't know which operation to use” instead of making it mandatory before every operation.

The current [catalog input](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/blob/e893667173c6b1d69099a97239313cf43cc399fb/packages/twenty-server/src/engine/core-modules/tool-provider/tools/get-tool-catalog.tool.ts#L13-L20) supports category filtering, but no search query, result limit or pagination. The [exposed MCP tools](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/blob/e893667173c6b1d69099a97239313cf43cc399fb/packages/twenty-server/src/engine/api/mcp/services/mcp-protocol.service.ts#L220-L285) don't include a capability-search tool.

Could the catalog accept a query and result limit, or could a small search tool return relevant operations? For example:

```text
search_tools(query, domain?, limit=5)
→ operation names and short descriptions
→ learn_tools for the selected operations
→ execute_tool
```

We saw the related work in [#21183](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/21183) and [#22875](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/22875). Hopefully these findings help show the effect on real agent tasks.

Happy to share sanitized traces and rerun the same scenarios against a change. We can compare discovery calls per task, response sizes and task outcomes.

title: An application creating a PRIVATE core workflow produces a workspace-readable one
body:
`createCoreWorkflow` stores `createdByUserWorkspaceId: userWorkspaceId`, and an application-authenticated call has no user workspace, so the row lands with a null owner. `buildCoreWorkflowVisibilityWhere` treats a null owner as readable by everyone (the clause exists so a workflow outlives its creator leaving the workspace), so a workflow an application asked to be PRIVATE is readable, and claimable, by every member with workflow access.

The same applies to duplicating a private workflow through an application token.

Both halves are on main today: the resolver carries `UserOrApplicationAuthGuard`, the input accepts `PRIVATE`, and the null-owner clause predates it. Either applications should be refused PRIVATE visibility, or private workflows need an ownership model that survives a non-user principal (owning application, say).

Found by greptile in review of https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/26158, where it is not a regression.

title: Safari: every click or keypress shows a `Cancelled` snackbar after opening Settings → MCP & APIs
body:
### Environment

- v2.41.0, self-hosted via the official Docker Compose (server, worker, postgres:16, redis)
- Safari, logged in

### What happens

After visiting **Settings → MCP & APIs**, every subsequent click or keypress anywhere in the app pops a snackbar reading `Cancelled` in the bottom-right corner. It keeps happening for the life of the tab and stops as soon as the window is closed and reopened. Chrome and Firefox never show it. Nothing actually fails — the requests in question were cancelled deliberately.

### Cause

Two things combine.

**1. The rejection handler matches on the error name only.** From the built bundle:

```js
const a = r?.networkError?.name === "AbortError" || r?.name === "AbortError";
const s = r instanceof Error && isChunkLoadError(r);
!a && !s && enqueueToast(...)   // raw error.message is shown here
```

WebKit does not name a cancelled request's rejection `AbortError` — it rejects with the message `Cancelled` and a different name — so the guard misses and the raw message reaches the user. Chromium names it `AbortError`, which is why this is Safari-only.

**2. `SettingsRestPlayground` leaves a request in flight.** The chunk creates an `AbortController`-backed `fetch` and has no cleanup path (no abort on unmount). Leaving the page leaves the request outstanding, and later interactions abort it — one snackbar per abort. That is why the page has to be visited once before the behaviour starts, and why a fresh tab is clean.

### Suggested fix

In the rejection handler, detect aborts by something browser-independent — the `AbortSignal`'s `aborted` flag, or `DOMException` with `name === "AbortError"` plus a message check — rather than the name alone. Separately, aborting the playground's controller on unmount would stop the rejections being generated at all.

### Related

- #14780 added the `AbortError` interception this guard is based on.
- #23571 fixed the same handler leaking a raw browser string on iOS Safari, but only for stale chunk-load errors.

title: A front component cannot preventDefault on an event
body:
### What happens

A front component's event handler runs on the other side of the thread boundary. By the time it receives the event, the event is serialized data — calling `preventDefault()` there reaches nothing, because the host has already returned and the browser has already run the default action.

The practical case is a textarea used as a message composer. `keydown:Enter` should send the message and not insert a newline, but the newline always wins: the guest cannot suppress it.

### Why it matters

There is no workaround inside the component. What is left is compensating after the fact — tracking the keystroke and undoing the value the browser already inserted — which is fragile and has to be rewritten in every component that needs it.

The host already suppresses the default for two specific cases (`onSubmit` on forms and `onDragOver` on drop targets, via `preventDefaultThenForwardToRemote`), so the mechanism exists; it just cannot be reached from a component for any other event.

### What would resolve it

Let an element declare which events it wants suppressed — `keydown:Enter`, `keydown:Shift+Enter`, and so on — so the host reads the rule synchronously while it still holds the real event, and the component keeps saying what it wants rather than how to get it.

title: IMAP: drafts pile up in the thread because every client autosave creates a new row and old drafts are never removed
body:
## Summary

On a self-hosted instance with an IMAP mailbox, a single reply appears as several draft rows in the email thread. Each save in the mail client adds one more row, and the old rows never disappear.

The IMAP driver never reports deleted (expunged) messages, and the import path only inserts, so it never updates or removes an existing row.

## Environment

- Twenty v2.39.0, self-hosted with Docker, image `twentycrm/twenty:v2.39.0`
- Mail server: Dovecot, IMAP over TLS on port 993
- Mail client: hoster webmail client (not sure what the use)
- The server advertises `CONDSTORE`, `QRESYNC`, `UIDPLUS` and `MOVE` after login

## What I see

The thread timeline in twenty shows each draft autosave as a new row. The IMAP messages behind those rows no longer exist. A `UID SEARCH` for that subject in `Drafts` returns nothing.

## Expected behavior

One draft row that holds the latest version, removed once the mail is sent or the draft deleted.

## Technical inputs

**Reproduce:**

1. Connect an IMAP mailbox whose client rewrites a draft on every save, meaning it appends a new message and expunges the old one. The trace below shows what that looks like.
2. Write a mail in the client and save it a few times, or let it autosave.
3. Let Twenty run its message import between the saves.
4. Open the thread in Twenty.


**IMAP trace:**

Read-only test with `EXAMINE` and `UID FETCH` on one new draft.

| Time (UTC) | `Drafts` HIGHESTMODSEQ | Event |
|---|---|---|
| 12:40:15 | 643 | new uid 2884, flags `(\Seen \Draft)`, message-id `<1297733633.357470...>` |
| 12:41:20 | 651 | new uid 2886 `<239981072.357555...>`, uid 2884 gone |
| 12:42:30 | 660 | new uid 2889 `<500785936.357672...>`, uid 2886 gone |
| 12:44:05 | 666 | new uid 2891 `<1955339940.357847...>`, uid 2889 gone |
| 13:08:06 | 672 | new uid 2893 `<856918606.359828...>`, uid 2891 gone |

UIDVALIDITY stayed at `1752657694` for the whole test. Every save creates a new UID and a new Message-ID, and the server deletes the previous one. The client skipped some UIDs in between, 2885, 2887 and 2888, which were further autosaves. The folder holds one message, but it already sits at UID 2893, so this client has created and deleted roughly 2,900 drafts in that folder.

Neither the external id, which is `folder:uid`, nor `headerMessageId` stays stable across a draft save. Every save looks like a new message to Twenty.

Happy to share more data privately if it helps fix the bug.


**Claudes suggestion:**

haven't checked it, because I'm not that good of a coder. Paths below are relative to
`packages/twenty-server/src/modules/messaging/`.

`message-import-manager/drivers/imap/services/imap-get-message-list.service.ts`
returns a hardcoded `messageExternalIdsToDelete: []` in both return paths, at
L109-115 and L157-163. It builds external ids as `${prefix}:${uid}` at L153-155.

`message-import-manager/drivers/imap/services/imap-sync.service.ts` only looks
forward. `fetchNewMessageUids` at L57-77 does this:

```ts
const lastSyncedUid = previousCursor?.highestUid ?? 0;
if (lastSyncedUid >= maxUid) { return []; }
const uidRange = `${lastSyncedUid + 1}:${maxUid}`;
```

`validateUidValidity` at L37-55 only throws when UIDVALIDITY changes. The driver
handles no expunge and no QRESYNC `VANISHED` response, although this server
advertises QRESYNC.

The import then only inserts. `services/messaging-message-list-fetch.service.ts`
at L162-181 skips every external id that already has an association, and
`services/messaging-message.service.ts` at L160-201 and L261 inserts only when
neither a message, matched by `headerMessageId`, nor an association exists. It
never updates `isDraft`, `text` or `receivedAt` on a row that already exists.

Five saves therefore produce five rows, and Twenty deletes or refreshes none of
them.

title: renewApplicationToken throttles only successful renewals, failed ones bypass the rate limit
body:
## Scope & Context

`renewApplicationToken` in `packages/twenty-server/src/engine/core-modules/application/application-oauth/application-oauth.resolver.ts` verifies the refresh token and checks its session binding *before* consuming the rate limit bucket. Malformed, expired or mismatched tokens therefore throw without ever consuming a token, so only successful renewals are throttled.

A caller holding a valid workspace session can loop on bad refresh tokens and trigger an unbounded number of JWT verifications. Each one runs `resolveVerificationKey` plus `jwt.verify` in `JwtWrapperService.verifyJwtToken`, so the work is not free.

This predates [#26191](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/26191). On `main` the mutation has no rate limit at all, so failed renewals were already unthrottled. That PR adds the first limit this mutation has ever had, but places it after validation, which leaves the failing path uncovered. Raised by Greptile while reviewing it.

The sibling OAuth endpoint already does it the other way round: `oauth-token.controller.ts` calls `applyRateLimit` as the first statement of every grant handler, keyed on IP, before any validation.

## Technical inputs

The current bucket key includes `applicationId`, which is only known once the token is decoded, so it cannot simply be moved up. Add a session scoped bucket before validation and keep the per-application one where it is:

```ts
await this.throttlerService.tokenBucketThrottleOrThrow(
  `app-renew:${workspaceId}:${userWorkspaceId}`,
  1,
  APPLICATION_TOKEN_RATE_LIMIT_MAX,
  APPLICATION_TOKEN_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS,
);

const applicationRefreshTokenPayload =
  await this.applicationTokenService.validateApplicationRefreshTokenForSessionOrThrow({
    applicationRefreshToken,
    workspaceId,
    userId: user.id,
    userWorkspaceId,
  });
```

- The mutation runs behind `WorkspaceAuthGuard` and `RequireAccessTokenGuard`, so `workspaceId` and `userWorkspaceId` are always available before any token parsing.
- Add an integration test asserting that repeated failed renewals consume the bucket and eventually return the throttler error, next to `packages/twenty-server/test/integration/metadata/suites/application/failing-application-token-renewal.integration-spec.ts`.

Depends on [#26191](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/26191) landing first, since the throttle it reorders is introduced there.

title: Kanban board does not show records created outside the board
body:
## Summary

A Kanban (board) view does not show a record created outside the board itself.
The record is in the database and a table view of the same object shows it
immediately; the board keeps its stale contents until the page is reloaded.
Switching to another view and back does not clear it.

There are **two independent defects** behind that one symptom, and they need
separate fixes:

1. **Board on screen when the record is created** — the create event reaches
   the board, which then decides not to refetch unless the new record sorts
   above the first card already loaded in its column.
2. **Board not on screen when the record is created** — the more common case
   in practice: you are on a record page adding a task. The board is unmounted,
   so nothing hears the event at all, and when you navigate back the board
   re-renders the ids it loaded last time instead of re-querying.

The built-in Tasks **By Status** view is where most people will meet this,
because the standard task-creation flows request `position: 'last'`, which is
exactly the case defect 1 ignores.

Reproduced against v2.37.0 (self-hosted, Docker). Both code paths are unchanged
on `main` as of 2026-09-19 — `RecordBoardQueryEffect.tsx` still gates the board
query on `queryIdentifierHasChanged || recordGroupIdsHaveChanged` with no
unmount cleanup, so both defects reproduce there as described.

## Reproduction

**Single tab (defect 2).** No second tab, no second device:

1. Open Tasks and select the built-in **By Status** Kanban.
2. Navigate to an Opportunity (or any record), open its **Tasks** tab, and add
   a task with **New task**.
3. Navigate back to Tasks. The Kanban does not show the new task. Switching to
   the table view shows it; switching back to the Kanban still does not.
4. Reload the page. It appears.

**Two tabs (defect 1).** Tab A on a Tasks table view, tab B on the By Status
Kanban; create a task from the "+" row at the bottom of the table in tab A.
Tab A shows the row; tab B never does until reloaded.

Two contrasts narrow the cause:

- Creating from the board's **own** column button does show the card — that
  path writes the id into the column's state directly
  (`useCreateNewIndexRecord.ts:135-148`), bypassing the event handler.
- Creating from the column header "+" or the command menu also works — those
  send `position: 'first'`, the one case defect 1 accepts.

Both defects were reproduced headlessly with Playwright against a fresh
workspace seeded with three To-do tasks, and both patches below verified
against the same scripts:

    defect 2 (single tab, task added from a record page)
      task created: position 6, status TODO
      visible-after-returning-to-board: false   → true with the patch
      visible-in-table-view:            true
      visible-after-view-switch-back:   false   → true with the patch
      visible-after-reload:             true

    defect 1 (board on screen, created via API with position: 'last')
      created: position 4, status TODO
      appeared-without-reload: false            → true (~1s) with the patch
      appeared-after-reload:   true

The table/Kanban split in defect 2 is the signature: the same record, in the
same tab, at the same moment, present in one view and absent from the other.
For defect 1 the board was polled for 15 seconds — far longer than the SSE
round trip, which lands in about a second once fixed. Fixing either defect did
not regress the other.

## Root cause

Both defects come from one design fact: **a board's records are not in the
Apollo cache.** They are fetched by an imperative grouped query with
`fetchPolicy: 'no-cache'`
(`object-record/record-index/hooks/useRecordIndexGroupsRecordsLazyGroupBy.ts:83`)
and held per column in Jotai component state that outlives the component. A
table's records are an Apollo **watched** query
(`object-record/hooks/useFindManyRecords.ts:94`), so any cache write re-renders
it. The board has to be told explicitly, twice over: while it is mounted, and
again when it is remounted.

### Defect 2 — the board is not mounted when the record is created

This is the single-tab case, and nothing about it involves SSE. Creating a task
from a record page dispatches the create event while the board is unmounted, so
`RecordBoardDataChangedEffect` is not listening. On the way back,
`RecordBoardQueryEffect.tsx:85-93` re-runs the board query only when

    queryIdentifierHasChanged || recordGroupIdsHaveChanged

Returning to the same view with the same filters and sorts changes neither.
`lastRecordBoardQueryIdentifierComponentState` is keyed to the board instance
and survives the unmount, so the comparison says "nothing changed" and the
column ids loaded minutes ago are rendered again. Switching to the table view
and back does not help for the same reason, while the table is correct because
it reads the Apollo cache, which the create did update.

### Defect 1 — the board is mounted and ignores the event

Both views receive the same SSE database event, turned into the same browser
event. What they do with `create-one` differs:

- **Table** —
  `record-table/virtualization/components/RecordTableVirtualizedDataChangedEffect.tsx:50`:
  every operation that is not an update falls into an `else` that refetches.
  A create always refreshes the table.
- **Board** — `record-board/components/RecordBoardDataChangedEffect.tsx:85`:
  a create refetches only if the record's `position` is the string `'first'`
  (:86), or its column is currently empty (:131), or

      createdRecordPosition < (firstExistingRecordInGroup.position ?? 0)   // :146

  Otherwise the handler falls through and does nothing at all.

The premise of that guard is that a record sorting after the first loaded card
is below the fold, and pagination will pick it up. Both halves fail here:

1. **Board columns are ordered by `position` ascending.** With no sort on the
   view, `turnSortsIntoOrderBy.ts` appends `position: 'AscNullsFirst'` as the
   only ordering, and the seeded "By Status" view defines no sorts. A record
   created at the end of the list therefore always fails the `<` test.
2. **That is what the creation flows ask for.** `position: 'last'` is sent by
   `activities/hooks/useOpenCreateActivityDrawer.ts:74` (New task from a record
   page), `object-record/record-list/components/RecordListAddNew.tsx:91`, and
   `record-table/components/RecordTableNoRecordGroupAddNew.tsx:54`.
3. **Pagination never rescues it.** A column returning fewer than
   `RECORD_BOARD_QUERY_PAGE_SIZE` (10) records sets its fetch-more flag to
   `false` (`useTriggerRecordBoardInitialQuery.ts:152`), so a short column
   issues no further query. The card cannot appear until a full re-query.

Small columns are the worst case, which is most boards in a small workspace.

## Suggested fix

Two patches, one per defect. Both are verified by the runs above.

### For defect 2 — make a remount re-query (10 lines)

The board's ids outlive the component, so the identifier that gates the query
should not. Clearing it on unmount makes the next mount behave like a first
mount. In `RecordBoardQueryEffect.tsx`, alongside the existing effect:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  return () => {
    setLastRecordBoardQueryIdentifier('');
  };
}, [setLastRecordBoardQueryIdentifier]);
```

`''` is the state's own default, so this restores the first-mount path rather
than inventing one. The cost is one grouped query when you return to a board,
which is what the table already pays on remount.

### For defect 1 — refetch when the column is fully loaded (21 lines)

The distinction the guard needs already exists per column:
`recordBoardShouldFetchMoreInColumnComponentFamilyState` is set to `false`
whenever a column comes back short, by both
`useTriggerRecordBoardInitialQuery.ts:152` and
`useTriggerRecordBoardFetchMore.ts:191`. A column that is fully loaded must
render any new record belonging to it, whatever its position.

In `RecordBoardDataChangedEffect.tsx`, after the group definition is resolved
(~line 127):

```tsx
const columnIsFullyLoaded = !store.get(
  recordBoardShouldFetchMoreInColumnCallbackState(
    recordGroupDefinitionFromGroupValue.id,
  ),
);

if (columnIsFullyLoaded) {
  triggerRecordBoardInitialQuery({ shouldResetScroll: false });
  return;
}
```

with the matching import, the `useAtomComponentFamilyStateCallbackState(...)`
binding (the hook is already imported in that file), and the dependency-array
entry. This keeps the existing optimization for genuinely paginated columns
rather than reverting it.

The blunter alternative for defect 1 — dropping the heuristic so any create
refetches, which is what the table does — is a one-line change, but it
refetches every column on every create, including large boards where the
current behaviour is right.

## Known limitation the patches do not address

When the view has sorts, columns are ordered by the sort field first and
`position` only as a tiebreak, so comparing positions is comparing the wrong
key: a record created at the end can still belong at the top of a sorted
column. The fully-loaded condition makes this harmless for short columns, but a
long, sorted, paginated column can still miss a card. Deciding that properly
means evaluating the view's sort against the created record, which is a larger
change and deliberately out of scope here.

title: Engine-provisioned "Go to {objectLabelPlural}" command menu items resolve to the wrong object's label, and junction objects get non-functional ones
body:
Environment: Self-hosted, v2.39.5

Background: Since [#23795](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty/pull/23795) (merged 2026-08-31), the metadata side-effect engine unconditionally provisions a "Go to {objectLabelPlural}" command-menu item (engineComponentKey: NAVIGATION) for every object, including junction/relation objects that have no navigable index page of their own.

Bug 1 — label collision: In a workspace with an object and its junction tables (e.g. Lead, plus junctions LeadContact, LeadOccupation, LeadAddress), the command menu shows multiple "Go to X" entries that all display the same resolved label instead of their own. Confirmed via direct DB inspection — 4 separate commandMenuItem rows exist, each with a distinct navigationTargetObjectMetadataId pointing at a different object (lead, leadContact, leadOccupation, leadAddress), all sharing the literal, unresolved label value "Go to {objectLabelPlural}". The frontend should interpolate each command's own target object's plural label independently, but instead all of them render as "Go to Leads." Reproduced in both a normal window and incognito, ruling out client-side cache — this points to a resolution/memoization bug keyed too broadly (likely on engineComponentKey alone rather than each command's own id or navigationTargetObjectMetadataId).

Bug 2 — non-functional for junction objects: Junction/relation objects have no sidebar entry or standalone index page in normal use. Their auto-provisioned "Go to X" command has nowhere sensible to navigate to, so clicking it does nothing.

To reproduce:

Create a custom object with at least one many-to-many relation (so a junction object is auto-created).
Open the command menu (⌘K).
Search for "Go to" — observe multiple entries with identical labels, one per junction plus the base object.
Click one of the junction-targeting entries — nothing happens.
Suggested fix directions:

Resolve each NAVIGATION command's label independently by its own navigationTargetObjectMetadataId, not a shared/memoized value.
Consider whether junction objects (already excluded from normal navigation/sidebar) should get a NAVIGATION command provisioned at all, or should at least default isActive: false.

title: Removing a connected account silently makes its messages disappear (no FK on messageChannelMessageAssociation.messageChannelId)
body:
# Removing a connected account silently makes its messages disappear (no FK on messageChannelMessageAssociation.messageChannelId)

**Version:** v2.39.5 (self-hosted, Docker)
**Severity:** silent data loss on a routine, documented user action

## Summary

Removing and re-adding a connected account deletes its `messageChannel` rows but
leaves every `messageChannelMessageAssociation` pointing at the now-deleted
channel. The server then **drops every message whose channel cannot be resolved**
from API responses. The messages are still in the database; they simply cease to
exist as far as the product is concerned. No error, no warning, nothing in the
logs.

We lost visibility of **65,886 messages across ~30,000 threads** this way in a
single day, while asking our team to reconnect their mailboxes — which is the
remediation your own UI steers people toward when a sync fails.

## Root cause

`messageChannelMessageAssociation` lives in the workspace schema;
`messageChannel` lives in `core`. The association's sibling columns have
cascades, but the channel column has no constraint at all:

```
FK on "messageId"        -> workspace_xxx.message(id)       ON DELETE CASCADE
FK on "messageThreadId"  -> workspace_xxx."messageThread"(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
FK on "messageChannelId" -> (none)
```

Verified with:

```sql
select conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid)
  from pg_constraint
 where conrelid = 'workspace_xxx."messageChannelMessageAssociation"'::regclass
   and contype = 'f';
```

Because nothing references `core."messageChannel"`, deleting a channel neither
cascades to the associations nor is refused. They are left dangling.

The dangling rows are then fatal at read time, in
`packages/twenty-server/src/modules/messaging/common/query-hooks/message/apply-messages-visibility-restrictions.service.ts`:

```ts
const messageChannels = associations
  .map((association) => messageChannelMap.get(association.messageChannelId))
  .filter(isDefined);

if (messageChannels.length === 0) {
  messages.splice(i, 1);   // <- the message is removed from the response
  continue;
}
```

"I cannot resolve this message's channel" is treated as "this message does not
exist", rather than as an error or a restricted-content state.

## Reproduction

1. Connect a Google account and let it sync some mail.
2. In **Settings → Accounts → Emails**, remove the account.
3. Add the same account again (this is the standard fix for a failed sync).
4. Open a contact you had corresponded with, or the Emails tab.

Expected: the previously imported history is still visible, or at minimum an
error explains why it is not.

Actual: the old messages are gone from every API response. In the database:

```sql
select count(*)
  from workspace_xxx."messageChannelMessageAssociation" a
 where not exists (
   select 1 from core."messageChannel" c where c.id = a."messageChannelId");
-- 65886
```

## Why this is worse than it first looks

- **It is triggered by the recommended remediation.** A mailbox in
  `FAILED_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS` cannot be fixed by retrying; the account has
  to be removed and re-added. So the fix for one problem silently causes a worse
  one.
- **The new channel does not recover the history.** It starts empty and imports
  only recent mail, so the gap is permanent without manual repair.
- **The link is unrecoverable by design.** Nothing records which mailbox a
  channel belonged to. Once the row is deleted, the only way to work out where
  65,886 orphaned associations should point is to inspect participant addresses
  and infer it. We had to do exactly that.
- **It is completely silent.** No exception, no log line, no empty state. The
  product just shows less mail than it did yesterday.

## Suggested fixes

Any one of these would prevent the data loss; the first two are the real fix.

1. **Declare the foreign key.** A cross-schema FK is valid in Postgres. With
   `ON DELETE CASCADE` the associations are cleaned up honestly; with
   `ON DELETE RESTRICT` the deletion is refused until they are handled. Either
   is better than dangling rows.
2. **Repoint on re-add.** When an account is reconnected for a handle that
   previously had a channel, migrate the existing associations to the new
   channel rather than abandoning them. This is what a user expects
   "reconnect my mailbox" to mean.
3. **Do not treat unresolvable as nonexistent.** In
   `applyMessagesVisibilityRestrictions`, an association pointing at a missing
   channel is a data-integrity problem, not a permissions outcome. Log it and
   either surface the message or mark it restricted — but do not silently splice
   it out of the response.

## Notes

We have worked around this with an external job that records
`channelId -> handle` while channels exist and repoints orphaned associations
onto the current channel for the same mailbox. That covers our own instance but
cannot fix the underlying integrity gap, and every self-hosted user reconnecting
a mailbox is exposed to it.

Related: the same `splice`/early-return style in the email thread UI makes a
permission gap render as a blank panel with no error. Filed separately.

Identifiers and addresses above are placeholders.

title: IMAP backfill deadlocks permanently when a batch is entirely filtered out (internal-only mail)
body:
## Summary

On a self-hosted instance, an IMAP backfill can stop making progress **permanently** while reporting itself healthy. The channel stays `ACTIVE`, `throttleFailureCount` is 0, nothing is logged above `log` level, and each cycle reports a correct, unchanging `toImportCount`.

The cause is that a batch of messages which `filterEmails` removes *in its entirety* is never recorded as processed. Because `messageChannelMessageAssociation` rows are only written for messages that survive filtering, the same UIDs are re-listed on every subsequent cycle, and the importer fetches and discards the identical batch forever.

This is distinct from #24826 (a `modSeq`/`highestUid` cursor invariant): here the cursor is fine and the list fetch is correct — the queue simply can never advance past a fully-filtered batch.

## Mechanism

In `messaging-messages-import.service.js`:

```js
const messagesToSave = filterEmails(/* … */);
if (messagesToSave.length > 0) {
  // only here are messages + associations persisted
}
```

`filterEmails` applies `filterOutIcsAttachments` → `filterOutUnsubscribeRequests` → `filterOutBlocklistedMessages` → `filterOutInternals` → group-email filtering.

`filterOutInternals` drops any message where **every** participant shares the account's own domain, and it is active whenever the handle is a work email and the workspace has `isInternalMessagesImportEnabled = false`:

```js
const shouldFilterOutInternals = isWorkEmail(primaryHandle) && !isInternalMessagesImportEnabled;
```

Note it has no sent-by-user exemption, unlike the group-email filter below it — so internal mail in the **Sent** folder is filtered too.

When a whole batch is internal-only:

1. `messagesToSave` is empty, so nothing is persisted and **no associations are created**
2. `messaging-message-list-fetch.service` computes the import set by excluding `existingMessageChannelMessageAssociationsExternalIds`, so those UIDs are still "missing"
3. They are re-queued on the next cycle, fetched again, filtered again — indefinitely

Progress halts at whatever UID the fully-filtered batch begins.

## Evidence

15-year Gmail mailbox, `[Gmail]/Sent Mail` = 40,407 messages, `SELECTED_FOLDERS` (sent only), `contactAutoCreationPolicy = SENT`.

Stuck at **exactly 22,144 imported messages for hours**. Meanwhile the log repeated:

```
[ImapMessageParserService] Fetched and parsed 400 messages from [Gmail]/Sent Mail in 32630ms
[MessagingMessageListFetchService] Is full sync: true, toImportCount: 40407, toDeleteCount: 0
[MessagingMessageListFetchService] Total messages to import count: 18263
```

400 messages fetched and parsed per pass, `18263` outstanding every pass, stored count never changing. `throttleFailureCount = 0`, blocklist empty, no errors. A clean 3-minute observation window with nothing else running confirmed 400 fetched / 0 saved.

**Confirmation of cause:** setting `workspace.isInternalMessagesImportEnabled = true` unblocked it immediately — +210 messages within 100 seconds, and the backfill resumed normally. No other change.

## Expected

Messages that are intentionally filtered out should still advance the queue — e.g. by writing an association (or an explicit "skipped" marker) for them, or by advancing the folder cursor past a fully-filtered batch. As it stands, any batch that filters to empty is an unrecoverable stall, and the only workaround is to relax the filter that caused it.

## Related observations from the same backfill

These may warrant separate issues; noting them here for context.

**1. Queued IDs appear to be lost on a transient IMAP error.** A dropped connection surfaces as:

```
ERROR [ImapMessagesImportErrorHandler] IMAP: Error importing message [Gmail]/Sent Mail:11431: {"code":"NoConnection"}
ERROR [MessagingMessagesImportService] Error (TEMPORARY_ERROR) importing messages: IMAP network error: Connection not available
```

After this the pending-import cache key (`messages-to-import:<ws>:<channel>`) is **gone**, the channel returns to `MESSAGE_LIST_FETCH_PENDING`, and because the cursor is already advanced the next (incremental) fetch finds nothing. The backfill cannot resume without `messaging:reset-channel`. Completing a large backfill therefore required an external supervisor re-running reset + trigger once per cycle. Default `MESSAGING_MESSAGES_GET_BATCH_SIZE=400` held one connection open 26–36s; reducing it to 100 made drops less frequent.

**2. No full sync ran on initial connection.** For a freshly connected mailbox (~1.1M messages in All Mail), every cycle logged `Is full sync: false` while per-folder cursors already held `highestUid` at the mailbox maximum — so all history was treated as already seen. Only **627 of 40,407** sent messages were imported before the channel went idle and reported healthy. `messaging:reset-channel` fixed it, after which `Is full sync: true, toImportCount: 40407`. Symptomatically different from #24826, but possibly the same family.

## Environment

- Twenty **2.39.5**, self-hosted Docker (`twentycrm/twenty:v2.39.5`), `twenty-server` + `twenty-worker`
- Postgres 16, Redis
- Gmail IMAP (app password), 68 folders (Gmail labels), `SELECTED_FOLDERS` → `[Gmail]/Sent Mail` only
- `contactAutoCreationPolicy = SENT`, `excludeNonProfessionalEmails = true`, `excludeGroupEmails = true`
- `isInternalMessagesImportEnabled = false` (the trigger condition)

title: Canonicalize internationalized email domains for storage and exact matching
body:
## Bug Description

Internationalized email domains are accepted but are stored and filtered as raw strings rather than a canonical IDNA representation. Semantically equivalent addresses can therefore fail exact matching and bypass the primary-email unique constraint.

For example, Twenty currently accepts both forms:

```text
admin@💩.la
admin@xn--ls8h.la
```

`💩.la` resolves to the ASCII IDNA form `xn--ls8h.la`, but an `eq`/`in` filter for one spelling does not match a record stored with the other spelling. Both spellings can also be stored as separate unique primary emails. Domain casing creates the same class of mismatch because email values are returned unchanged by validation and exact filters compile to raw PostgreSQL equality.

This was confirmed against current `main` by inspecting:

- `emailSchema`, which accepts Unicode email values.
- `validateEmailsPrimaryEmailSubfieldOrThrow`, which returns the original value without normalization.
- `computeWhereConditionParts`, where `eq` and `in` compare the supplied value directly.

Generic full-text/ILIKE search should not be used to solve identity matching: PostgreSQL tokenization removes characters such as the emoji from this example and can overmatch.

## Expected behavior

Twenty should apply one shared email canonicalization policy consistently:

- Canonicalize the domain at write time (trim, normalize domain separators/casing, and convert IDNs to ASCII/punycode).
- Apply the same canonicalization to incoming exact `eq`/`in` filters and other identity-match paths.
- Cover both primary and additional email values.
- Keep local-part normalization as an explicit product decision; domain canonicalization is independently required because DNS domains are case-insensitive and IDNA has equivalent Unicode/ASCII forms.
- Preserve human-friendly display input separately if retaining the original Unicode spelling is desired.

After canonicalization, `admin@💩.la` and `admin@xn--ls8h.la` should resolve to the same identity and uniqueness key.

## Technical inputs

- Prefer a shared canonicalizer in the EMAILS field layer so GraphQL/REST writes, imports, exact filters, duplicate detection, and integrations cannot diverge.
- Preserve indexed equality for exact matching rather than falling back to `ILIKE`.
- A migration must detect existing canonical collisions before enforcing canonical uniqueness. For example, a workspace may already contain one person under each spelling above.
- Add tests for Unicode IDNs, their punycode equivalents, domain case, Unicode dot variants/trailing dots, primary emails, additional emails, and `eq`/`in` filters.

title: Record page FieldsWidget groups (viewFieldGroups) stay isActive=false forever for objects that existed before the 2.20 grouping feature - Fields sidebar renders flat instead of sectioned
body:
### Environment
- Self-hosted, Docker deploy (`twentyhq/twenty` fork, `--target twenty` image)
- Upgraded a pre-2.20 workspace (~v2.18, June 2026 baseline) straight to v2.38.1 via `yarn command:prod upgrade`
- Bug reproduces on an otherwise-clean upgrade (also verified with the fix from #24003-style guard applied to the 2-20 `create-message-list-view` command, unrelated to this issue)

### Symptom
After upgrading, the record page "Fields" sidebar renders as a **flat, ungrouped list** (no section headers) for some standard objects (Company, Opportunity) while others (Person, Task, Note, ...) correctly show their sectioned groups (General/Business/Contact/System, etc.).

`getViews(viewTypes: [FIELDS_WIDGET])` returns `viewFieldGroups: []` for the affected views, even though `core.viewFieldGroup` rows for those views clearly exist and are correctly associated (`viewId` matches, no soft-delete).

### Root cause
The affected `viewFieldGroup` rows all have `isActive = false`, with `createdAt` timestamps from **before** the workspace was ever upgraded past 2.20 (i.e. from before the FieldsWidget/viewFieldGroup grouping feature existed for that workspace). The upgrade-version-command that backfills/activates the default record-page FieldsWidget view for existing objects apparently never sets `isActive = true` on these pre-existing rows.

`createViewFieldGroupsByViewIdLoader` (packages/twenty-server/.../dataloader.service.ts) does:
```ts
return findManyFlatEntityByIdInFlatEntityMaps({ ... })
  .filter((g) => g.deletedAt === null && g.isActive)   // <- silently drops inactive groups
  .map(fromFlatViewFieldGroupToViewFieldGroupDto);
```
So the group IDs are correctly listed on the parent `flatView.viewFieldGroupIds`, but every group object itself gets filtered out because `isActive` is `false`. Traced this end-to-end with temporary debug logging in `WorkspaceFlatViewMapCacheService` and `WorkspaceFlatViewFieldGroupMapCacheService` - the flat maps are computed correctly from the DB, `isActive: false` is exactly what's stored.

Manually running:
```sql
UPDATE core."viewFieldGroup" SET "isActive" = true WHERE "workspaceId" = '...' AND "isActive" = false;
```
plus `yarn command:prod cache:flat-cache-invalidate --all-metadata --workspace-id ...` fixes the display immediately.

### Second, related bug: the fix doesn't stick
Calling `upsertFieldsWidget` to add/edit a **custom** viewFieldGroup on the same view (e.g. adding a new "Financials" section next to the standard ones) resets `isActive` back to `false` on the pre-existing standard groups of that view every time - as if some reconciliation step re-touches them and fails to (re)activate them. This happened twice, reproducibly, in our testing (see `isActive` flip back to `false` on "Deal"/"Relations"/"Details"/"General"/"Business"/"Contact"/"System" immediately after two separate `upsertFieldsWidget` calls that only referenced the new custom group).

Also worth noting: attempting to include one of the *pre-existing standard* groups' real `id` directly in an `upsertFieldsWidget` call errors with:
```
Migration action 'create' for 'viewFieldGroup' (universalIdentifier: ...) failed: duplicate key value violates unique constraint ... Key (id)=(...) already exists.
```
i.e. the migration diff logic treats an existing standard group as "to create" rather than "to update", which may be the same underlying issue causing the `isActive` reset.

### Reproduction
1. Have a workspace originally provisioned before the FieldsWidget/viewFieldGroup feature (pre-2.20).
2. Upgrade it past 2.20 (any way).
3. Query `getViews(viewTypes: [FIELDS_WIDGET])` for a standard object like Company/Opportunity - `viewFieldGroups` comes back empty even though the DB rows exist.
4. Fix `isActive`, confirm sections render.
5. Call `upsertFieldsWidget` to add a new group to the same view - the pre-existing groups' `isActive` flips back to `false`.

Happy to share the (temporary, since removed) debug-logging patches used to trace this if useful.

title: In-memory rich text ILIKE filter ignores SQL wildcards in RLS predicate evaluation
body:
sql ILIKE treats `%` and `_` as wildcards and a backslash escapes the next char, but the in-memory mirror for rich text in `packages/twenty-shared/src/utils/filter/utils/isMatchingRichTextFilter.ts` does not follow the same rules, so a rich text filter can grant a row in postgres and deny it in memory (or the other way round)

three gaps on current main:

1. `_` is never translated, it stays a literal underscore
2. `%` is translated to `.*` but the regex has no `s` flag, so it does not match line terminators, while postgres `%` matches any sequence including newlines
3. a markdown leaf without `ilike` matches only the empty string in memory, while postgres `ILIKE null` is never true and matches nothing

repro on main:

\`\`\`ts
// postgres: SELECT 'abc' ILIKE 'a_c' -> true
isMatchingRichTextFilter({ richTextFilter: { markdown: { ilike: "a_c" } }, value: "abc" }) // false in memory, should be true
\`\`\`

this matters on the update path: the enterprise rls predicate (`is-record-matching-rls-row-level-permission-predicate.util.ts`) routes RICH_TEXT fields through `isMatchingRichTextFilter`, so a rule with `_` or a multiline `%` pattern denies updates the database predicate would grant

fix incoming in #25505

title: batchTriggerAndWait parent never resumes after all child runs complete (batch stuck in PROCESSING with runs: [])
body:
### Provide environment information

- Trigger.dev Cloud, project `proj_puwcdoxtxcywuaznmabj`, prod env, region us-east-1
- `@trigger.dev/sdk` 4.5.14, `@trigger.dev/build` 4.5.14
- Node 22, deployed version `20260921.61`

### Describe the bug

A task that calls `batchTriggerAndWait` never resumed after every child run in the batch reached `COMPLETED`. The parent stayed frozen (no attempt error, `durationMs: 0`, no output) for ~95 minutes until we cancelled it by hand.

Three parent runs of the same task (`scheduled-metrics-orchestration`) hit this in one wave on 2026-09-21. Their siblings (17 other runs of the same task, same code, same batch sizes) resumed normally within a minute of their children completing.

Two shapes were observed:

**1. Batch stuck in `PROCESSING` although all its runs finished** (2 of 3 cases)

`GET /api/v1/batches/{id}` still returns `status: "PROCESSING"` and `runs: []` hours after every child run completed:

| Parent run | Batch | runCount | Batch created | Last child `finishedAt` | Batch status now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `run_06gccj5uiktpn7mrncb3mki501` | `batch_06gcclsm9uuel78rsk0jsgoa01` | 562 | 2026-09-21T23:40:24Z | 2026-09-21T23:41:13Z | `PROCESSING`, `runs: []`, `updatedAt` 23:40:24Z |
| `run_06gccj5ugpgo8odb5kr8incm01` | `batch_06gcclu8fqilo4lfhncod8b401` | 76 | 2026-09-21T23:40:36Z | 2026-09-21T23:41:01Z | `PROCESSING`, `runs: []`, `updatedAt` 23:40:37Z |

All 562 (resp. 76) child runs show `status: COMPLETED` under the parent's `relatedRuns.children`, and each child carries the batch id above. The batch record itself never transitioned out of `PROCESSING`, so it looks like the batch's run list was never sealed and the parent's waitpoint was never completed.

**2. Batch `COMPLETED`, parent still never resumed** (1 of 3 cases)

| Parent run | Batch | runCount | Batch `updatedAt` | Parent resumed? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `run_06gccj5uhhi8a3998loq7v9e01` | `batch_06gcclodi3fqtidru2fmj8bt01` | 529 | 2026-09-21T23:40:42Z (`status: COMPLETED`, 529 run ids listed) | No — frozen until cancelled 2026-09-22T01:14:01Z |

All three parents were created at 2026-09-21T23:28:33Z from one `batchTriggerAndWait` of 20 items (`batch_06gccj5sinpguml4d39lrfi101`) issued by the cron task `social-metrics-collection` run `run_06gccic2vbemcv2j2okvr9t801`. Cancelling the three frozen parents (`Canceled by user`, 01:14–01:19Z) is what finally let the grandparent's batch wait resolve.

### Reproduction

We cannot reproduce on demand. It happened to 3 of 20 concurrent parents doing the same thing: `await childTask.batchTriggerAndWait(items)` with 470–580 items per batch, each item carrying an idempotency key and a small JSON payload. Parent task has `maxDuration: 300`, child `maxDuration: 600`, each on its own queue with a concurrency limit.

### Expected behavior

Once every run in the batch is in a final state the batch should be marked complete and the waiting parent should be resumed (or, if the batch record cannot be sealed, the parent should fail with an error rather than wait forever).

### Additional information

Happy to share more run ids or grant dashboard access to the project if that helps.

title: bug: self-hosted webapp cannot obtain IRSA credentials — fast-xml-parser 5.7.x rejects @aws-sdk/xml-builder's addEntity("#xD")
body: ## Summary On a self-hosted deployment on EKS, annotating the `trigger-webapp` service account for IRSA makes every AWS call from the webapp fail during **credential resolution**. The pinned `fast-xml-parser@5.7.1` throws while the AWS SDK configures its XML parser, so the STS `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` response can never be deserialized. The most visible symptom is that magic-link login email fails every time — which locks users out completely when email is the only configured auth provider. ## Error ``` Failed to send email to , Magic sign-in link for Trigger.dev. Error Error: [EntityReplacer] Invalid character '#' in entity name: "#xD" Deserialization error: to see the raw response, inspect the hidden field {error}.$response on this object. {"message":"Error sending magic link email","level":"error"} ``` Stack: ``` at fast-xml-parser@5.7.1 … setExternalEntities at fast-xml-parser@5.7.1 … parse at @aws-sdk/xml-builder@3.930.0/dist-cjs/xml-parser.js:17 … parseXML at @aws-sdk/core@3.940.0 … XmlShapeDeserializer.parseXml at @aws-sdk/core@3.940.0 … AwsQueryProtocol.deserializeResponse ``` The STS response itself is HTTP 200 and well formed — it contains no character references and the string `#xD` appears nowhere in it. The throw happens while *configuring* the parser, not while reading the document, so it is entirely content-independent. ## Cause `@aws-sdk/xml-builder@3.930.0/dist-cjs/xml-parser.js` registers two character references as entities: ```js parser.addEntity("#xD", "\r"); parser.addEntity("#10", "\n"); ``` `fast-xml-parser` 5.7.0 tightened entity-name validation to reject `#`, so `setExternalEntities` throws on every `parse()` call. ## Minimal reproduction (no AWS credentials, no network) ```js const { XMLParser } = require('fast-xml-parser'); const parser = new XMLParser({ htmlEntities: true }); parser.addEntity('#xD', '\r'); // exactly what @aws-sdk/xml-builder does parser.parse('1', true); // throws on 5.7.0 and 5.7.1 ``` ## Affected versions | fast-xml-parser | Result | | --- | --- | | 4.5.6 | ok | | 5.6.0 | ok | | **5.7.0** | **throws** | | **5.7.1** | **throws** | | 5.8.0 | ok | | 5.9.3 / 5.10.1 / 5.11.0 / 5.11.1 | ok | Broken only in 5.7.0–5.7.1, fixed in 5.8.0. ## Why this affects every current release `pnpm-lock.yaml` pins `fast-xml-parser@5.7.1` on `v4.5.9`, `v4.5.11`, `v4.5.13`–`v4.5.16`, `v4.6.0`–`v4.6.3` and `main`. No published image avoids the broken window, so operators cannot work around it by moving image tags. The repo also resolves `fast-xml-parser@4.5.6` for the older `@aws-sdk/xml-builder@3.821.0`. Which copy a given client resolves to decides whether it works: the ECR push path keeps working, while `@aws-sdk/client-sesv2@3.940.0` (which pulls `xml-builder@3.930.0`) does not. That makes the failure look service-specific when it is really protocol-specific — every awsQuery/XML service, STS included, is affected. ## Impact Any self-hosted deployment using IRSA. Because STS uses the awsQuery (XML) protocol, credential resolution itself fails, so this is not limited to email — it breaks every AWS call made through the affected SDK copy. Deployments using node/instance credentials are unaffected, since IMDS returns JSON and never touches the XML parser. That is why the problem appears only once a pod is switched to IRSA, and why it can sit latent for a long time before surfacing. ## Suggested fix Force a non-affected version: ```jsonc // package.json "pnpm": { "overrides": { "fast-xml-parser": "^5.8.0" } } ``` ## Environment - `ghcr.io/triggerdotdev/trigger.dev:v4.6.0`, Helm chart, self-hosted on EKS - Node 24 - `EMAIL_TRANSPORT=aws-ses` - Credentials via IRSA (service account annotated with `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn`) Possibly related: #3364 (service-account annotation support for IRSA).

title: feat: move remaining bundled images off bitnamilegacy (postgresql, redis, kubectl sidecar)
body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Chart `4.5.15` still pulls four images from the `bitnamilegacy/*` namespace. Broadcom froze that namespace when Bitnami moved to a paid catalogue — those tags no longer receive security patches, so the Debian base layers accumulate CVEs indefinitely with no upgrade path.

From `values.yaml` in chart 4.5.15:

| Values path | Image |
|---|---|
| `postgres.image.repository` | `bitnamilegacy/postgresql:17.5.0-debian-12-r12` |
| `redis.image.repository` | `bitnamilegacy/redis:8.0.2-debian-12-r4` |
| `s3.image.repository` | `bitnamilegacy/minio:2025.6.13-debian-12-r0` |
| `s3.console.image.repository` | `bitnamilegacy/minio-object-browser:2.0.2-debian-12-r0` |
| `webapp.tokenSyncer.image.repository` | `bitnamilegacy/kubectl:1.28` |

The first four come from Bitnami subchart dependencies (`postgresql` 16.7.14, `redis` 21.2.6, `minio` 17.0.9 via the `s3` alias). The fifth is a first-party chart value.

**`bitnamilegacy/kubectl:1.28` is worth calling out separately.** kubectl supports roughly ±1 minor version of skew against the API server. Pinned at 1.28, the token-syncer sidecar is already outside that window on any cluster running 1.30+, and increasingly so over time. It is also the only one of the five that is not tied to a subchart, so it is a one-line values change.

This affects every self-hosted deployment that uses the bundled datastores, which is the chart's default (`postgres.deploy`, `redis.deploy` and `s3.deploy` are all `true`).

## Describe the solution you'd like to see

The same treatment ClickHouse received in 4.5.15 — first-party templates using the upstream official image, with `digest` support for reproducible pinning:

```yaml
clickhouse:
  image:
    registry: docker.io
    repository: clickhouse/clickhouse-server
    tag: "26.2"
    digest: ""
```

That change was handled well: `persistence.existingClaim` auto-detects the PVC the Bitnami subchart left behind, a `data-paths.xml` ConfigMap points the server at the directory the old layout used, and a chown init container relabels the volume for the new uid — including on storage classes where `fsGroup` cannot relabel. Migrating from the bundled Bitnami ClickHouse was genuinely seamless as a result.

Applying the same pattern to postgres and redis would remove the remaining exposure. Upstream official images exist for both (`postgres`, `redis`, or `valkey`), and for the sidecar `registry.k8s.io/kubectl` is the upstream-maintained option.

Order of value, in our view:

1. **`webapp.tokenSyncer.image`** — no subchart, no state, no migration. A values change.
2. **redis** — stateful but largely reconstructible.
3. **postgresql** — highest value and highest care required, since it holds the secret store and run state.

## Describe alternate solutions

**Override the subchart images in values.** Not viable in practice: the Bitnami charts assume Bitnami's filesystem layout, entrypoints and uid conventions, so substituting an official image breaks the probes and init scripts. We looked at this and discounted it.

**Point the chart at external services** (`deploy: false`). This works and is what we have done for object storage — `s3.deploy: false` with `s3.external.*` removed both MinIO images cleanly. But it is not a general answer: it pushes every self-hoster toward managed Postgres and Redis, which defeats much of the point of a self-hosted chart, and the bundled path stays unpatched for everyone who does not.

**Stay on `bitnamilegacy` and accept the risk.** Defensible only while these services are cluster-internal with no ingress, which is the common case. It still shows up in image scanning and in security questionnaires, and it degrades over time as CVEs accumulate against frozen base layers.

## Additional information

Related prior work:

- #4249 — deploy ClickHouse from the official image instead of Bitnami (the precedent this asks to extend)
- #4197 — ClickHouse writers require CH ≥25.8 while the chart bundled ClickHouse 25

Verified against chart `4.5.15` (`oci://ghcr.io/triggerdotdev/charts/trigger`) and against a running self-hosted deployment on k3s, where `kubectl get pods -o jsonpath` over the namespace confirms the five images above are what actually run.

Happy to test a pre-release chart against a live single-node self-hosted install if that is useful — we have just completed the 4.4.6 → 4.5.15 upgrade including the ClickHouse volume adoption, so the migration path is fresh.

title: feat: first-class helper for Standard Webhooks (Svix) signature verification
body:
**Title** : `feat: first-class helper for Standard Webhooks (Svix) signature verification`

**Labels** : enhancement

---

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I'm building event-driven automations where Trigger.dev jobs react to webhook events emitted by **Composio** (and a growing number of other providers that have adopted the [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com/) spec — Stripe, GitHub, Slack, Linear, etc.). Composio sends three headers (`webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature: v1,<base64>`) and the signature is HMAC-SHA256 over `${id}.${timestamp}.${raw_body}` with the secret base64-decoded and a tolerance window (default 300s).

The built-in `verifyRequestSignature` helper only covers single-header schemes (Stripe/GitHub/Cal.com/Novu style), so it can't validate Standard Webhooks signatures out of the box. I get why — supporting every provider's signature scheme isn't Trigger.dev's job, and the helper is the right escape hatch for ad-hoc cases.

The friction isn't the helper itself; it's that **every Trigger.dev user integrating with a Standard Webhooks provider ends up writing the same ~50 lines of crypto + header parsing** in their `verify` lambda. That's the part that feels like it could live in the SDK.

## Describe the solution you'd like to see

A first-class helper that handles the Standard Webhooks signature scheme, roughly:

```ts
import { verifyStandardWebhooks, STANDARD_WEBHOOKS_TOLERANCE_SECONDS } from "@trigger.dev/sdk";

const endpoint = client.defineHttpEndpoint({
  id: "composio",
  source: "composio.dev",
  verify: async (request) => {
    return await verifyStandardWebhooks({
      request,
      secret: process.env.COMPOSIO_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
      // optional, defaults to 300s per the Standard Webhooks spec
      tolerance: STANDARD_WEBHOOKS_TOLERANCE_SECONDS,
    });
  },
});
```

What the helper should cover:

- Read `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature` headers
- Validate the `v1,` signature prefix (and tolerate future `v1a,`/`v1b,` variants if the spec adds them)
- Base64-decode the secret before HMAC
- Compute `HMAC-SHA256(secret, ${id}.${timestamp}.${raw_body})` with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`
- Enforce the timestamp tolerance window (anti-replay)
- Return the same `{ success: true }` / `{ success: false, reason: "..." }` shape as `verifyRequestSignature` so it's a drop-in

Bonus if it also exposes the parsed, verified payload (mirroring what the Composio SDK does on its `verifyWebhook` return type) — that lets users skip the manual `JSON.parse` after `success: true`.

## Describe alternate solutions

I considered a few:

1. **PR my own implementation into the SDK.** I can do this, but the vouched-contributor + changesets + single-feature-per-PR process makes it heavier than a feature request first. And honestly I'd rather the maintainers pick the API shape — `verifyStandardWebhooks` vs. a generic `verifyWebhook({ scheme: "standard-webhooks", ... })` flag, where in the helper tree it lives, etc.
2. **Publish a separate community package** (`@trigger-dev-community/standard-webhooks-verify`). Viable, but the moment Trigger.dev ships its own helper, the community package dies. Putting it upstream also makes it discoverable next to `verifyRequestSignature`.
3. **Move the verification outside Trigger.dev.** A small service in front of Trigger.dev that does the verification + republishes to a queue that Trigger.dev jobs subscribe to. Works, but it's exactly the kind of workaround that disappears when the gap closes. I'd rather not maintain it if I don't have to — and it pushes trust boundaries out of the SDK, which is the opposite of where they belong.

## Additional information

**Adoption is broader than it looks.** Standard Webhooks isn't a niche format — it's becoming the de facto signature spec for SaaS webhooks:

- **Big-name migrations to Standard Webhooks**: Stripe, GitHub, Slack, Linear, Shopify (via Svix)
- **Svix-native providers**: most new B2B SaaS that use Svix as their delivery layer (Resend, Novu, Knock, Courier, ngrok, Composio, etc.)
- **Spec is actively maintained**: the Standard Webhooks org publishes reference SDKs in Node, Python, Go, Ruby, Java, .NET, Rust, PHP — so wrapping one of those in a Trigger.dev helper is low-risk and well-tested upstream crypto

That means a single helper in the SDK would unblock integrations with **every** provider in the list above — not just one. The same ~50 lines of crypto currently written by hand per integration become write-once-for-everyone.

**Why now** : the Standard Webhooks spec keeps winning — Stripe and GitHub both migrated to it; Linear, Svix-hosted providers, and a long tail of "send us webhooks" SaaS follow. Every new Standard Webhooks integration in Trigger.dev costs ~50 lines of boilerplate that the SDK could own.

I'm not blocked on this — my workaround works — but it felt worth flagging since the cost of closing the gap is low and the gain compounds with every new Standard Webhooks integration anyone tries to build.

**Spec references** :
- https://www.standardwebhooks.com/ — the spec
- https://docs.composio.dev/docs/webhook-verification — provider example that uses it
- https://github.com/standard-webhooks/standard-webhooks — reference implementations in multiple languages

title: LogicalReplicationClient stuck in infinite extend loop after Redlock expires; never re-acquires
body:
## Summary

`RunsReplicationService` / `LogicalReplicationClient` uses Redlock2 (Redis-based) for single-leader election on the `task_runs_to_clickhouse_v1` slot. When the leader loses its lock — typically a brief event-loop stall or Redis blip pushes lock renewal past `RUN_REPLICATION_LEADER_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` — the renewer never recovers. It just logs `Cannot extend an already-expired lock` every `RUN_REPLICATION_LEADER_LOCK_EXTEND_INTERVAL_MS` forever.

The pod stays "healthy" (no health check failure, no crash), but it's no longer functionally the leader. Another pod *does* eventually pick up the lock and resume replication, so user-visible CH lag is bounded — but the original pod permanently spams two paired error log lines per renewal interval.

## Environment

- Self-hosted Trigger.dev v4 (helm chart, `webapp` v4.3.0)
- 8 webapp replicas
- `RUN_REPLICATION_LEADER_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS=60000`
- `RUN_REPLICATION_LEADER_LOCK_EXTEND_INTERVAL_MS=20000`
- `RUN_REPLICATION_LEADER_LOCK_ADDITIONAL_TIME_MS=30000`
- Redis: bitnami chart, single master in same K8s cluster

## Observed log signature

Every 20 seconds, identical timestamp delta, from one specific pod:

```json
{
  "name":"LogicalReplicationClient",
  "slotName":"task_runs_to_clickhouse_v1",
  "publicationName":"task_runs_to_clickhouse_v1_publication",
  "error":{
    "message":"Cannot extend an already-expired lock.",
    "stack":"ExecutionError: Cannot extend an already-expired lock.\n    at Redlock2.extend (apps/webapp/build/index.js:120923:13)\n    at Lock.extend (apps/webapp/build/index.js:120834:25)\n    at Timeout._onTimeout (apps/webapp/build/index.js:121616:49)\n    at listOnTimeout (node:internal/timers:573:17)\n    at process.processTimers (node:internal/timers:514:7)"
  },
  "lockTimeoutMs":60000,
  "lockExtendIntervalMs":20000,
  "message":"Failed to extend leader lock",
  "level":"error"
}
```

Followed in the same millisecond by a sibling `RunsReplicationService` log:

```json
{
  "name":"RunsReplicationService",
  "error":{ "message":"Cannot extend an already-expired lock.", ... },
  "message":"Replication client error",
  "level":"error"
}
```

Sample timestamps from one production pod, no breaks for hours:

```
2026-04-23T03:14:12.639Z
2026-04-23T03:14:32.639Z
2026-04-23T03:14:52.639Z
2026-04-23T03:15:12.640Z
2026-04-23T03:15:32.640Z
…
```

Killing the pod (`kubectl delete pod`) immediately stops the spam. The newly-spawned replica re-elects cleanly.

## Reproduction

1. Self-host with multiple webapp replicas + Redis. Run `task_runs_to_clickhouse_v1` replication.
2. Force the current leader pod's event loop to stall for `> RUN_REPLICATION_LEADER_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS`. Easy ways:
   - `kubectl exec` and send `SIGSTOP` for 70 seconds, then `SIGCONT`. Or
   - Network-partition the pod from Redis for 70 seconds via NetworkPolicy.
3. After the partition heals, the renewer's next `extend()` call returns `Cannot extend an already-expired lock`.
4. Observe the log line repeating every `RUN_REPLICATION_LEADER_LOCK_EXTEND_INTERVAL_MS` indefinitely. The pod is no longer the leader (another pod has acquired the slot) but doesn't know it.

## Root cause (best guess from stack)

`LogicalReplicationClient.extend()` is invoked from a `setTimeout` chain with no error-handler that resets state. When `extend()` rejects:

- The error is caught and logged.
- The `setTimeout` for the next extend is re-armed unconditionally.
- The client never calls `acquire()` to re-elect, never disposes the slot listener, and never marks itself as not-leader.

So the renewal loop continues forever against a lock the pod no longer holds, while the actual leadership has silently moved to another pod.

## Suggested fix

In `RunsReplicationService` / `LogicalReplicationClient` extend handler, when `extend()` rejects with the expired-lock error:

1. Stop the renewal loop (`clearTimeout`).
2. Tear down the open replication slot subscription on this pod.
3. Either:
   - Attempt a fresh `acquire()` (will succeed if no other pod holds it, fail otherwise — fail is fine, just don't loop), OR
   - Throw / exit the process so K8s restarts and the deployment self-heals via a fresh re-election.

Option (b) is simpler and more robust against further state drift. The pod is already useless for replication at this point, so a restart costs nothing.

## Workaround for self-hosters

Restart the noisy pod. We've added a Datadog monitor on `Failed to extend leader lock` count > N/min that pages and includes a runbook step to `kubectl delete pod <leader>`.

## Related context

We're already running this CH-load reduction work that surfaced the issue: https://github.com/triggerdotdev/trigger.dev/issues/3426
